意富比神社 (船橋大神宮) | image = Oohi-jinja(Funabashi) Haiden.jpg | caption =The prayer area (''haisho'') before the shrine's ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|41|46.17|N|139|59|34.58|E|region:JP_type:landmark_scale:1000|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Amaterasu]] | founded_by = [[Yamato Takeru]] (legendary) | established = 40th year of the reign of [[Emperor Keikō]] (legendary) | date_destroyed = | location = 5-2-1, Miyamoto, [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]]
[[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]] 273-0003 | website = http://oohijinja.jp/index.html | architecture_style = ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' | festival = 20 October | leadership = }} '''Ōhi Shrine''' (意富比神社, ''Ōhi-jinja''; [[Historical kana orthography|historical orthography]]: ''Ohohi-jinja''), also known as '''Funabashi Daijingū''' (船橋大神宮), is a [[Shinto]] [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] dedicated to the [[Solar deity|sun goddess]] [[Amaterasu]] located in the city of [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]] in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. ==History== Legend claims that Ōhi Shrine was founded by the mythical hero [[Yamato Takeru]] during his campaign in eastern Japan in the 40th year of the reign of his father, [[Emperor Keikō]], to pray for the end of a drought that afflicted the area.{{cite web|title=About Oohi Jinja Shrine (Funabashi Daijingū Shrine)|url=http://oohijinja.jp/history-eng.html|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|accessdate=15 August 2017}}{{cite book |last1=Fujisawa |first1=Morihiko |title=日本伝説叢書 下総の巻 (Nihon Densetsu Sōsho: Shimōsa no Maki) |date=1919 |publisher=Nihon Densetsu Sōsho Kankōkai |pages=85–87 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/953575/62}}{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=259–261 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社 (Ōhi-jinja)|url=http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=%5E$&search:word=3061|access-date=2020-11-24|website=神社のひろば 神社探検隊！|publisher=Chiba Jinjachō}} The shrine first appears in the historical record as "Ōhi-no-Kami (意富比神) of [[Shimōsa Province]]" in the ''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (901), which records its promotion to higher [[List of Japanese court ranks, positions and hereditary titles|ranks]] ([[:ja:神階|神階]], ''shinkai'') by the imperial court in the mid-9th century, starting from 863 ([[Jōgan]] 5) when it was raised from the rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) to senior fifth, lower grade (正五位下). It was promoted again in 871 (Jōgan 13) to senior fifth rank, upper grade (正五位上), and finally in 874 (Jōgan 16) to junior fourth, lower grade (従四位下).{{cite web |title=日本三代實録 (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku) |website=J-TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館 |accessdate=2020-11-21 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519144319/http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html|url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html |archivedate=2018-05-19 |language=Japanese}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社（下総国葛飾郡）|url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/190201.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=Shinto Jinja Database|publisher=Kokugakuin University|language=Japanese}} It is listed as a "minor shrine" (小社, ''shōsha'') in the ''Jinmyōchō'' ("Register of Deities") section of the ''[[Engishiki]]'' (927 CE).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社|url=http://engishiki.org/shimousa/bun/smf200702-01.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=延喜式神社の調査}} While the shrine is currently dedicated to the imperial sun goddess [[Amaterasu]], one theory suggests that it may have originally venerated a local [[solar deity]] (the name ''Ōhi'' may be interpreted as meaning "great sun") who became conflated with Amaterasu during the medieval era. [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi]] and his son [[Minamoto no Yoshiie|Yoshiie]] is said to have rebuilt the shrine somewhere during the [[Tengi|Tengi era]] (1053-1058). In 1138 ([[Hōen]] 4), the area in which the shrine was located became a tribute estate or ''mikuriya'' (御厨) of the [[Grand Shrine of Ise]] known as 'Natsumi Mikuriya' (夏見御厨). The shrine became widely known as 'Funabashi Shinmei' (船橋神明) or 'Funabashi Ise Daijingū' (船橋伊勢大神宮) from the medieval period onwards, suggesting that the [[Shinto shrine#Famous shrines and shrine networks|branch]] of Ise Shrine (神明社, ''shinmeisha'') established within the estate was merged with it at some point. [[File:舩橋意富比神社 - Ōhi Shrine (Funabashi).jpg|thumb|left|430x430px|Ōhi Shrine during the [[Edo period]] (from the ''[[Edo meisho zue]]'')]][[Nichiren]], the founder of [[Nichiren Buddhism]], is said to have performed a ritual [[Fasting|fast]] at the shrine and offered a [[Gohonzon]] and a sword to it.{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=270–273 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}} At the beginning of the [[Edo period]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]] donated land worth fifty ''[[koku]]'' to the shrine. He is also said to have presented a wooden statue of Yamato Takeru to it in 1608 (Keichō 13). The statue was installed by Ieyasu's son and successor, [[Tokugawa Hidetada|Hidetada]], in a newly-constructed [[Setsumatsusha|auxiliary shrine]] in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8), in which he also enshrined [[Tōshō-gū|the deified spirit]] of his late father. Hidetada himself would later be enshrined there by his son [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]], the third ''[[shōgun]]'' of the [[Tokugawa shogunate|Tokugawa dynasty]].{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=262–263}} The shrine was destroyed during the [[:ja:市川・船橋戦争|Battle of Funabashi]] (part of the [[Boshin War]]) in 1868 ([[Keiō]] 4).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=灯明台|url=https://www.city.funabashi.lg.jp/kurashi/gakushu/0005/p008848.html|access-date=2020-11-23|website=Funabashi City Official Website|language=Japanese}} The main sanctuary (''[[honden]]'') was rebuilt in 1873 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] 6), with the ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' and other shrine buildings being rebuilt in 1923 ([[Taishō]] 12), 1963 ([[Shōwa (1926–1989)|Shōwa]] 38), 1975 (Shōwa 50), and 1985 (Shōwa 60), respectively. ==Structures== === Auxiliary shrines === The shrine contains a number of auxiliary shrines (''[[setsumatsusha]]'') within its precincts, some of which are: *'''Toyoukehime Shrine (豊受姫神社, ''Toyoukehime-jinja''), a.k.a. ''Gekū'' (外宮)''' :An auxiliary shrine dedicated to [[Toyoukebime|Toyoukehime]] (Toyouke-no-Ōkami), the goddess of the Outer Shrine (''Gekū'') of Ise. The shrine was renovated in 2015 using wood formerly used in the Inner Ise Shrine (''Naikū'').{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=豊受姫神社（外宮）竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/toyoukehimejinja-gaigu-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''Tokiwa Shrine (常盤神社)''' :Dedicated to [[Yamato Takeru]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]], and [[Tokugawa Hidetada]]. Originally established by Hidetada in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8) to enshrine Yamato Takeru and his father Ieyasu, he was also eventually enshrined alongside them as a deity by his son and successor [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]]. The current shrine building, replacing the previous one constructed during the Meiji period, was built in 2015 to commemorate the upcoming 400th anniversary of Ieyasu's death the following year.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=常磐神社竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/tokiwajinja-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}}{{Cite Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''[[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Shrine]] (金刀比羅社, ''Kotohira-sha'')''' *'''Funatama Shrine (船玉神社)''' :This boat-shaped shrine is currently dedicated to [[Kamiumi|Ame-no-Torifune]] In 1138 ([[Hōen]] 4), the area in which the shrine was located became a tribute estate or ''mikuriya'' (御厨) of the [[Grand Shrine of Ise]] known as 'Natsumi Mikuriya' (夏見御厨). The shrine became widely known as 'Funabashi Shinmei' (船橋神明) or 'Funabashi Ise Daijingū' (船橋伊勢大神宮) from the medieval period onwards, suggesting that the [[Shinto shrine#Famous shrines and shrine networks|branch]] of Ise Shrine (神明社, ''shinmeisha'') established within the estate was merged with it at some point. [[File:舩橋意富比神社 - Ōhi Shrine (Funabashi).jpg|thumb|left|430x430px|Ōhi Shrine during the [[Edo period]] (from the ''[[Edo meisho zue]]'')]][[Nichiren]], the founder of [[Nichiren Buddhism]], is said to have performed a ritual [[Fasting|fast]] at the shrine and offered a [[Gohonzon]] and a sword to it.{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=270–273 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}} At the beginning of the [[Edo period]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]] donated land worth fifty ''[[koku]]'' to the shrine. He is also said to have presented a wooden statue of Yamato Takeru to it in 1608 (Keichō 13). The statue was installed by Ieyasu's son and successor, [[Tokugawa Hidetada|Hidetada]], in a newly-constructed [[Setsumatsusha|auxiliary shrine]] in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8), in which he also enshrined [[Tōshō-gū|the deified spirit]] of his late father. Hidetada himself would later be enshrined there by his son [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]], the third ''[[shōgun]]'' of the [[Tokugawa shogunate|Tokugawa dynasty]].{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=262–263}} The shrine was destroyed during the [[:ja:市川・船橋戦争|Battle of Funabashi]] (part of the [[Boshin War]]) in 1868 ([[Keiō]] 4).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=灯明台|url=https://www.city.funabashi.lg.jp/kurashi/gakushu/0005/p008848.html|access-date=2020-11-23|website=Funabashi City Official Website|language=Japanese}} The main sanctuary (''[[honden]]'') was rebuilt in 1873 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] 6), with the ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' and other shrine buildings being rebuilt in 1923 ([[Taishō]] 12), 1963 ([[Shōwa (1926–1989)|Shōwa]] 38), 1975 (Shōwa 50), and 1985 (Shōwa 60), respectively. ==Structures== === Auxiliary shrines === The shrine contains a number of auxiliary shrines (''[[setsumatsusha]]'') within its precincts, some of which are: *'''Toyoukehime Shrine (豊受姫神社, ''Toyoukehime-jinja''), a.k.a. ''Gekū'' (外宮)''' :An auxiliary shrine dedicated to [[Toyoukebime|Toyoukehime]] (Toyouke-no-Ōkami), the goddess of the Outer Shrine (''Gekū'') of Ise. The shrine was renovated in 2015 using wood formerly used in the Inner Ise Shrine (''Naikū'').{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=豊受姫神社（外宮）竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/toyoukehimejinja-gaigu-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''Tokiwa Shrine (常盤神社)''' :Dedicated to [[Yamato Takeru]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]], and [[Tokugawa Hidetada]]. Originally established by Hidetada in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8) to enshrine Yamato Takeru and his father Ieyasu, he was also eventually enshrined alongside them as a deity by his son and successor [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]]. The current shrine building, replacing the previous one constructed during the Meiji period, was built in 2015 to commemorate the upcoming 400th anniversary of Ieyasu's death the following year.{{Cite 意富比神社 (船橋大神宮) | image = Oohi-jinja(Funabashi) Haiden.jpg | caption =The prayer area (''haisho'') before the shrine's ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|41|46.17|N|139|59|34.58|E|region:JP_type:landmark_scale:1000|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Amaterasu]] | founded_by = [[Yamato Takeru]] (legendary) | established = 40th year of the reign of [[Emperor Keikō]] (legendary) | date_destroyed = | location = 5-2-1, Miyamoto, [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]]
[[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]] 273-0003 | website = http://oohijinja.jp/index.html | architecture_style = ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' | festival = 20 October | leadership = }} '''Ōhi Shrine''' (意富比神社, ''Ōhi-jinja''; [[Historical kana orthography|historical orthography]]: ''Ohohi-jinja''), also known as '''Funabashi Daijingū''' (船橋大神宮), is a [[Shinto]] [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] dedicated to the [[Solar deity|sun goddess]] [[Amaterasu]] located in the city of [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]] in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. ==History== Legend claims that Ōhi Shrine was founded by the mythical hero [[Yamato Takeru]] during his campaign in eastern Japan in the 40th year of the reign of his father, [[Emperor Keikō]], to pray for the end of a drought that afflicted the area.{{cite web|title=About Oohi Jinja Shrine (Funabashi Daijingū Shrine)|url=http://oohijinja.jp/history-eng.html|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|accessdate=15 August 2017}}{{cite book |last1=Fujisawa |first1=Morihiko |title=日本伝説叢書 下総の巻 (Nihon Densetsu Sōsho: Shimōsa no Maki) |date=1919 |publisher=Nihon Densetsu Sōsho Kankōkai |pages=85–87 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/953575/62}}{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=259–261 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社 (Ōhi-jinja)|url=http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=%5E$&search:word=3061|access-date=2020-11-24|website=神社のひろば 神社探検隊！|publisher=Chiba Jinjachō}} The shrine first appears in the historical record as "Ōhi-no-Kami (意富比神) of [[Shimōsa Province]]" in the ''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (901), which records its promotion to higher [[List of Japanese court ranks, positions and hereditary titles|ranks]] ([[:ja:神階|神階]], ''shinkai'') by the imperial court in the mid-9th century, starting from 863 ([[Jōgan]] 5) when it was raised from the rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) to senior fifth, lower grade (正五位下). It was promoted again in 871 (Jōgan 13) to senior fifth rank, upper grade (正五位上), and finally in 874 (Jōgan 16) to junior fourth, lower grade (従四位下).{{cite web |title=日本三代實録 (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku) |website=J-TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館 |accessdate=2020-11-21 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519144319/http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html|url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html |archivedate=2018-05-19 |language=Japanese}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社（下総国葛飾郡）|url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/190201.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=Shinto Jinja Database|publisher=Kokugakuin University|language=Japanese}} It is listed as a "minor shrine" (小社, ''shōsha'') in the ''Jinmyōchō'' ("Register of Deities") section of the ''[[Engishiki]]'' (927 CE).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社|url=http://engishiki.org/shimousa/bun/smf200702-01.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=延喜式神社の調査}} While the shrine is currently dedicated to the imperial sun goddess [[Amaterasu]], one theory suggests that it may have originally venerated a local [[solar deity]] (the name ''Ōhi'' may be interpreted as meaning "great sun") who became conflated with Amaterasu during the medieval era. [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi]] and his son [[Minamoto no Yoshiie|Yoshiie]] is said to have rebuilt the shrine somewhere during the [[Tengi|Tengi era]] (1053-1058). In 1138 ([[Hōen]] 4), the area in which the shrine was located became a tribute estate or ''mikuriya'' (御厨) of the [[Grand Shrine of Ise]] known as 'Natsumi Mikuriya' (夏見御厨). The shrine became widely known as 'Funabashi Shinmei' (船橋神明) or 'Funabashi Ise Daijingū' (船橋伊勢大神宮) from the medieval period onwards, suggesting that the [[Shinto shrine#Famous shrines and shrine networks|branch]] of Ise Shrine (神明社, ''shinmeisha'') established within the estate was merged with it at some point. [[File:舩橋意富比神社 - Ōhi Shrine (Funabashi).jpg|thumb|left|430x430px|Ōhi Shrine during the [[Edo period]] (from the ''[[Edo meisho zue]]'')]][[Nichiren]], the founder of [[Nichiren Buddhism]], is said to have performed a ritual [[Fasting|fast]] at the shrine and offered a [[Gohonzon]] and a sword to it.{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=270–273 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}} At the beginning of the [[Edo period]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]] donated land worth fifty ''[[koku]]'' to the shrine. [[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]] 273-0003 | website = http://oohijinja.jp/index.html | architecture_style = ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' | festival = 20 October | leadership = }} '''Ōhi Shrine''' (意富比神社, ''Ōhi-jinja''; [[Historical kana orthography|historical orthography]]: ''Ohohi-jinja''), also known as '''Funabashi Daijingū''' (船橋大神宮), is a [[Shinto]] [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] dedicated to the [[Solar deity|sun goddess]] [[Amaterasu]] located in the city of [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]] in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. ==History== Legend claims that Ōhi Shrine was founded by the mythical hero [[Yamato Takeru]] during his campaign in eastern Japan in the 40th year of the reign of his father, [[Emperor Keikō]], to pray for the end of a drought that afflicted the area.{{cite web|title=About Oohi Jinja Shrine (Funabashi Daijingū Shrine)|url=http://oohijinja.jp/history-eng.html|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|accessdate=15 August 2017}}{{cite book |last1=Fujisawa |first1=Morihiko |title=日本伝説叢書 下総の巻 (Nihon Densetsu Sōsho: Shimōsa no Maki) |date=1919 |publisher=Nihon Densetsu Sōsho Kankōkai |pages=85–87 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/953575/62}}{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=259–261 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社 (Ōhi-jinja)|url=http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=%5E$&search:word=3061|access-date=2020-11-24|website=神社のひろば 神社探検隊！|publisher=Chiba Jinjachō}} The shrine first appears in the historical record as "Ōhi-no-Kami (意富比神) of [[Shimōsa Province]]" in the ''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (901), which records its promotion to higher [[List of Japanese court ranks, positions and hereditary titles|ranks]] ([[:ja:神階|神階]], ''shinkai'') by the imperial court in the mid-9th century, starting from 863 ([[Jōgan]] 5) when it was raised from the rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) to senior fifth, lower grade (正五位下). It was promoted again in 871 (Jōgan 13) to senior fifth rank, upper grade (正五位上), and finally in 874 (Jōgan 16) to junior fourth, lower grade (従四位下).{{cite web |title=日本三代實録 (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku) |website=J-TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館 |accessdate=2020-11-21 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519144319/http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html|url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html |archivedate=2018-05-19 |language=Japanese}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社（下総国葛飾郡）|url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/190201.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=Shinto Jinja Database|publisher=Kokugakuin University|language=Japanese}} It is listed as a "minor shrine" (小社, ''shōsha'') in the ''Jinmyōchō'' ("Register of Deities") section of the ''[[Engishiki]]'' (927 CE).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社|url=http://engishiki.org/shimousa/bun/smf200702-01.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=延喜式神社の調査}} While the shrine is currently dedicated to the imperial sun goddess [[Amaterasu]], one theory suggests that it may have originally venerated a local [[solar deity]] (the name ''Ōhi'' may be interpreted as meaning "great sun") who became conflated with Amaterasu during the medieval era. [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi]] and his son [[Minamoto no Yoshiie|Yoshiie]] is said to have rebuilt the shrine somewhere during the [[Tengi|Tengi era]] (1053-1058). In 1138 ([[Hōen]] 4), the area in which the shrine was located became a tribute estate or ''mikuriya'' (御厨) of the [[Grand Shrine of Ise]] known as 'Natsumi Mikuriya' (夏見御厨). The shrine became widely known as 'Funabashi Shinmei' (船橋神明) or 'Funabashi Ise Daijingū' (船橋伊勢大神宮) from the medieval period onwards, suggesting that the [[Shinto shrine#Famous shrines and shrine networks|branch]] of Ise Shrine (神明社, ''shinmeisha'') established within the estate was merged with it at some point. [[File:舩橋意富比神社 - Ōhi Shrine (Funabashi).jpg|thumb|left|430x430px|Ōhi Shrine during the [[Edo period]] (from the ''[[Edo meisho zue]]'')]][[Nichiren]], the founder of [[Nichiren Buddhism]], is said to have performed a ritual [[Fasting|fast]] at the shrine and offered a [[Gohonzon]] and a sword to it.{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=270–273 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}} At the beginning of the [[Edo period]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]] donated land worth fifty ''[[koku]]'' to the shrine. He is also said to have presented a wooden statue of Yamato Takeru to it in 1608 (Keichō 13). The statue was installed by Ieyasu's son and successor, [[Tokugawa Hidetada|Hidetada]], in a newly-constructed [[Setsumatsusha|auxiliary shrine]] in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8), in which he also enshrined [[Tōshō-gū|the deified spirit]] of his late father. Hidetada himself would later be enshrined there by his son [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]], the third ''[[shōgun]]'' of the [[Tokugawa shogunate|Tokugawa dynasty]].{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=262–263}} The shrine was destroyed during the [[:ja:市川・船橋戦争|Battle of Funabashi]] (part of the [[Boshin War]]) in 1868 ([[Keiō]] 4).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=灯明台|url=https://www.city.funabashi.lg.jp/kurashi/gakushu/0005/p008848.html|access-date=2020-11-23|website=Funabashi City Official Website|language=Japanese}} The main sanctuary (''[[honden]]'') was rebuilt in 1873 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] 6), with the ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' and other shrine buildings being rebuilt in 1923 ([[Taishō]] 12), 1963 ([[Shōwa (1926–1989)|Shōwa]] 38), 1975 (Shōwa 50), and 1985 (Shōwa 60), respectively. ==Structures== === Auxiliary shrines === The shrine contains a number of auxiliary shrines (''[[setsumatsusha]]'') within its precincts, some of which are: *'''Toyoukehime Shrine (豊受姫神社, ''Toyoukehime-jinja''), a.k.a. ''Gekū'' (外宮)''' :An auxiliary shrine dedicated to [[Toyoukebime|Toyoukehime]] (Toyouke-no-Ōkami), the goddess of the Outer Shrine (''Gekū'') of Ise. The shrine was renovated in 2015 using wood formerly used in the Inner Ise Shrine (''Naikū'').{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=豊受姫神社（外宮）竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/toyoukehimejinja-gaigu-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''Tokiwa Shrine (常盤神社)''' :Dedicated to [[Yamato Takeru]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]], and [[Tokugawa Hidetada]]. Originally established by Hidetada in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8) to enshrine Yamato Takeru and his father Ieyasu, he was also eventually enshrined alongside them as a deity by his son and successor [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]]. The current shrine building, replacing the previous one constructed during the Meiji period, was built in 2015 to commemorate the upcoming 400th anniversary of Ieyasu's death the following year.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=常磐神社竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/tokiwajinja-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2015-12-07|title=意富比神社（船橋大神宮）|url=https://jinja.tokyolovers.jp/chiba/funabashi/oohijinja|access-date=2020-11-27|website=神社と御朱印|language=ja}} *'''Yakumo Shrine (八雲神社, ''Yakumo-jinja'')''' :This shrine, located beside the ''Gekū'', enshrines [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]], [[Kushinadahime]], and [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi]] (Ōkuninushi). * '''Ōtori Shrine (大鳥神社, ''Ōtori-jinja'')''' :Dedicated to Yamato Takeru. *'''Ame-no-Mihashira Shrine (天之御柱宮, ''Ame-no-Mihashira-no-miya'')''' :Dedicated to the ''eirei'' (英霊, "heroic spirits") or war dead who lost their lives in service of Japan. *'''Yatsurugi Shrine (八劔神社, ''Yatsurugi-jinja'') and [[Yasaka Shrine]] (八坂神社, ''Yasaka-jinja'')''' :The two shrines, both dedicated to Susanoo, are in the form of two ''[[mikoshi]]'' housed within a single building.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=境内のご案内|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/guide/|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''[[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Shrine]] (金刀比羅社, ''Kotohira-sha'')''' *'''Funatama Shrine (船玉神社)''' :This boat-shaped shrine is currently dedicated to [[Kamiumi|Ame-no-Torifune]] and the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha|Sumiyoshi deities]], though the shrine's name suggests it may have originally venerated the ''[[:ja:船霊|funadama]]'' ("boat spirit"), a folk deity worshiped by fishermen and sailors as a protector of ships.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Funadama|url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/bts/bts_f.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Basic Terms of 意富比神社 (船橋大神宮) | image = Oohi-jinja(Funabashi) Haiden.jpg | caption =The prayer area (''haisho'') before the shrine's ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|41|46.17|N|139|59|34.58|E|region:JP_type:landmark_scale:1000|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Amaterasu]] | founded_by = [[Yamato Takeru]] (legendary) | established = 40th year of the reign of [[Emperor Keikō]] (legendary) | date_destroyed = | location = 5-2-1, Miyamoto, [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]]
[[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]] 273-0003 | website = http://oohijinja.jp/index.html | architecture_style = ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' | festival = 20 October | leadership = }} '''Ōhi Shrine''' (意富比神社, ''Ōhi-jinja''; [[Historical kana orthography|historical orthography]]: ''Ohohi-jinja''), also known as '''Funabashi Daijingū''' (船橋大神宮), is a [[Shinto]] [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] dedicated to the [[Solar deity|sun goddess]] [[Amaterasu]] located in the city of [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]] in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. ==History== Legend claims that Ōhi Shrine was founded by the mythical hero [[Yamato Takeru]] during his campaign in eastern Japan in the 40th year of the reign of his father, [[Emperor Keikō]], to pray for the end of a drought that afflicted the area.{{cite web|title=About Oohi Jinja Shrine (Funabashi Daijingū Shrine)|url=http://oohijinja.jp/history-eng.html|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|accessdate=15 August 2017}}{{cite book |last1=Fujisawa |first1=Morihiko |title=日本伝説叢書 下総の巻 (Nihon Densetsu Sōsho: Shimōsa no Maki) |date=1919 |publisher=Nihon Densetsu Sōsho Kankōkai |pages=85–87 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/953575/62}}{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=259–261 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社 (Ōhi-jinja)|url=http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=%5E$&search:word=3061|access-date=2020-11-24|website=神社のひろば 神社探検隊！|publisher=Chiba Jinjachō}} The shrine first appears in the historical record as "Ōhi-no-Kami (意富比神) of [[Shimōsa Province]]" in the ''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (901), which records its promotion to higher [[List of Japanese court ranks, positions and hereditary titles|ranks]] ([[:ja:神階|神階]], ''shinkai'') by the imperial court in the mid-9th century, starting from 863 ([[Jōgan]] 5) when it was raised from the rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) to senior fifth, lower grade (正五位下). It was promoted again in 871 (Jōgan 13) to senior fifth rank, upper grade (正五位上), and finally in 874 (Jōgan 16) to junior fourth, lower grade (従四位下).{{cite web |title=日本三代實録 (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku) |website=J-TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館 |accessdate=2020-11-21 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519144319/http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html|url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html |archivedate=2018-05-19 |language=Japanese}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社（下総国葛飾郡）|url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/190201.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=Shinto Jinja Database|publisher=Kokugakuin University|language=Japanese}} It is listed as a "minor shrine" (小社, ''shōsha'') in the ''Jinmyōchō'' ("Register of Deities") section of the ''[[Engishiki]]'' (927 CE).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社|url=http://engishiki.org/shimousa/bun/smf200702-01.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=延喜式神社の調査}} While the shrine is currently dedicated to the imperial sun goddess [[Amaterasu]], one theory suggests that it may have originally venerated a local [[solar deity]] (the name ''Ōhi'' may be interpreted as meaning "great sun") who became conflated with Amaterasu during the medieval era. [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi]] and his son [[Minamoto no Yoshiie|Yoshiie]] is said to have rebuilt the shrine somewhere during the [[Tengi|Tengi era]] (1053-1058). In 1138 ([[Hōen]] 4), the area in which the shrine was located became a tribute estate or ''mikuriya'' (御厨) of the [[Grand Shrine of Ise]] known as 'Natsumi Mikuriya' (夏見御厨). The shrine became widely known as 'Funabashi Shinmei' (船橋神明) or 'Funabashi Ise Daijingū' (船橋伊勢大神宮) from the medieval period onwards, suggesting that the [[Shinto shrine#Famous shrines and shrine networks|branch]] of Ise Shrine (神明社, ''shinmeisha'') established within the estate was merged with it at some point. [[File:舩橋意富比神社 - Ōhi Shrine (Funabashi).jpg|thumb|left|430x430px|Ōhi Shrine during the [[Edo period]] (from the ''[[Edo meisho zue]]'')]][[Nichiren]], the founder of [[Nichiren Buddhism]], is said to have performed a ritual [[Fasting|fast]] at the shrine and offered a [[Gohonzon]] and a sword to it.{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=270–273 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}} At the beginning of the [[Edo period]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]] donated land worth fifty ''[[koku]]'' to the shrine. He is also said to have presented a wooden statue of Yamato Takeru to it in 1608 (Keichō 13). The statue was installed by Ieyasu's son and successor, [[Tokugawa Hidetada|Hidetada]], in a newly-constructed [[Setsumatsusha|auxiliary shrine]] in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8), in which he also enshrined [[Tōshō-gū|the deified spirit]] of his late father. Hidetada himself would later be enshrined there by his son [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]], the third ''[[shōgun]]'' of the [[Tokugawa shogunate|Tokugawa dynasty]].{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=262–263}} The shrine was destroyed during the [[:ja:市川・船橋戦争|Battle of Funabashi]] (part of the [[Boshin War]]) in 1868 ([[Keiō]] 4).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=灯明台|url=https://www.city.funabashi.lg.jp/kurashi/gakushu/0005/p008848.html|access-date=2020-11-23|website=Funabashi City Official Website|language=Japanese}} The main sanctuary (''[[honden]]'') was rebuilt in 1873 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] 6), with the ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' and other shrine buildings being rebuilt in 1923 ([[Taishō]] 12), 1963 ([[Shōwa (1926–1989)|Shōwa]] 38), 1975 (Shōwa 50), and 1985 (Shōwa 60), respectively. ==Structures== === Auxiliary shrines === The shrine contains a number of auxiliary shrines (''[[setsumatsusha]]'') within its precincts, some of which are: *'''Toyoukehime Shrine (豊受姫神社, ''Toyoukehime-jinja''), a.k.a. ''Gekū'' (外宮)''' :An auxiliary shrine dedicated to [[Toyoukebime|Toyoukehime]] (Toyouke-no-Ōkami), the goddess of the Outer Shrine (''Gekū'') of Ise. The shrine was renovated in 2015 using wood formerly used in the Inner Ise Shrine (''Naikū'').{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=豊受姫神社（外宮）竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/toyoukehimejinja-gaigu-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''Tokiwa Shrine (常盤神社)''' :Dedicated to [[Yamato Takeru]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]], and [[Tokugawa Hidetada]]. Originally established by Hidetada in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8) to enshrine Yamato Takeru and his father Ieyasu, he was also eventually enshrined alongside them as a deity by his son and successor [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]]. The current shrine building, replacing the previous one constructed during the Meiji period, was built in 2015 to commemorate the upcoming 400th anniversary of Ieyasu's death the following year.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=常磐神社竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/tokiwajinja-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2015-12-07|title=意富比神社（船橋大神宮）|url=https://jinja.tokyolovers.jp/chiba/funabashi/oohijinja|access-date=2020-11-27|website=神社と御朱印|language=ja}} *'''Yakumo Shrine (八雲神社, ''Yakumo-jinja'')''' :This shrine, located beside the ''Gekū'', enshrines [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]], [[Kushinadahime]], and [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi]] (Ōkuninushi). * '''Ōtori Shrine (大鳥神社, ''Ōtori-jinja'')''' :Dedicated to Yamato Takeru. *'''Ame-no-Mihashira Shrine (天之御柱宮, ''Ame-no-Mihashira-no-miya'')''' :Dedicated to the ''eirei'' (英霊, "heroic spirits") or war dead who lost their lives in service of Japan. *'''Yatsurugi Shrine (八劔神社, ''Yatsurugi-jinja'') and [[Yasaka Shrine]] (八坂神社, ''Yasaka-jinja'')''' :The two shrines, both dedicated to Susanoo, are in the form of two ''[[mikoshi]]'' housed within a single building.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=境内のご案内|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/guide/|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''[[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Shrine]] (金刀比羅社, ''Kotohira-sha'')''' *'''Funatama Shrine (船玉神社)''' :This boat-shaped shrine is currently dedicated to [[Kamiumi|Ame-no-Torifune]] and the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha|Sumiyoshi deities]], though the shrine's name suggests it may have originally venerated the ''[[:ja:船霊|funadama]]'' ("boat spirit"), a folk deity worshiped by fishermen and sailors as a protector of ships.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Funadama|url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/bts/bts_f.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Basic Terms of The statue was installed by Ieyasu's son and successor, [[Tokugawa Hidetada|Hidetada]], in a newly-constructed [[Setsumatsusha|auxiliary shrine]] in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8), in which he also enshrined [[Tōshō-gū|the deified spirit]] of his late father. Hidetada himself would later be enshrined there by his son [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]], the third ''[[shōgun]]'' of the [[Tokugawa shogunate|Tokugawa dynasty]].{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=262–263}} The shrine was destroyed during the [[:ja:市川・船橋戦争|Battle of Funabashi]] (part of the [[Boshin War]]) in 1868 ([[Keiō]] 4).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=灯明台|url=https://www.city.funabashi.lg.jp/kurashi/gakushu/0005/p008848.html|access-date=2020-11-23|website=Funabashi City Official Website|language=Japanese}} The main sanctuary (''[[honden]]'') was rebuilt in 1873 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] 6), with the ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' and other shrine buildings being rebuilt in 1923 ([[Taishō]] 12), 1963 ([[Shōwa (1926–1989)|Shōwa]] 38), 1975 (Shōwa 50), and 1985 (Shōwa 60), respectively. ==Structures== === Auxiliary shrines === The shrine contains a number of auxiliary shrines (''[[setsumatsusha]]'') within its precincts, some of which are: *'''Toyoukehime Shrine (豊受姫神社, ''Toyoukehime-jinja''), a.k.a. ''Gekū'' (外宮)''' :An auxiliary shrine dedicated to [[Toyoukebime|Toyoukehime]] (Toyouke-no-Ōkami), the goddess of the Outer Shrine (''Gekū'') of Ise. The shrine was renovated in 2015 using wood formerly used in the Inner Ise Shrine (''Naikū'').{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=豊受姫神社（外宮）竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/toyoukehimejinja-gaigu-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''Tokiwa Shrine (常盤神社)''' :Dedicated to [[Yamato Takeru]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]], and [[Tokugawa Hidetada]]. Originally established by Hidetada in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8) to enshrine Yamato Takeru and his father Ieyasu, he was also eventually enshrined alongside them as a deity by his son and successor [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]]. The current shrine building, replacing the previous one constructed during the Meiji period, was built in 2015 to commemorate the upcoming 400th anniversary of Ieyasu's death the following year.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=常磐神社竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/tokiwajinja-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2015-12-07|title=意富比神社（船橋大神宮）|url=https://jinja.tokyolovers.jp/chiba/funabashi/oohijinja|access-date=2020-11-27|website=神社と御朱印|language=ja}} *'''Yakumo Shrine (八雲神社, ''Yakumo-jinja'')''' :This shrine, located beside the ''Gekū'', enshrines [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]], [[Kushinadahime]], and [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi]] (Ōkuninushi). * '''Ōtori Shrine (大鳥神社, ''Ōtori-jinja'')''' :Dedicated to Yamato Takeru. *'''Ame-no-Mihashira Shrine (天之御柱宮, ''Ame-no-Mihashira-no-miya'')''' :Dedicated to the ''eirei'' (英霊, "heroic spirits") or war dead who lost their lives in service of Japan. *'''Yatsurugi Shrine (八劔神社, ''Yatsurugi-jinja'') and [[Yasaka Shrine]] (八坂神社, ''Yasaka-jinja'')''' :The two shrines, both dedicated to Susanoo, are in the form of two ''[[mikoshi]]'' housed within a single building.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=境内のご案内|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/guide/|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''[[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Shrine]] (金刀比羅社, ''Kotohira-sha'')''' *'''Funatama Shrine (船玉神社)''' :This boat-shaped shrine is currently dedicated to [[Kamiumi|Ame-no-Torifune]] and the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha|Sumiyoshi deities]], though the shrine's name suggests it may have originally venerated the ''[[:ja:船霊|funadama]]'' ("boat spirit"), a folk deity worshiped by fishermen and sailors as a protector of ships.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Funadama|url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/bts/bts_f.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Basic Terms of [[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]] 273-0003 | website = http://oohijinja.jp/index.html | architecture_style = ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' | festival = 20 October | leadership = }} '''Ōhi Shrine''' (意富比神社, ''Ōhi-jinja''; [[Historical kana orthography|historical orthography]]: ''Ohohi-jinja''), also known as '''Funabashi Daijingū''' (船橋大神宮), is a [[Shinto]] [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] dedicated to the [[Solar deity|sun goddess]] [[Amaterasu]] located in the city of [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]] in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. ==History== Legend claims that Ōhi Shrine was founded by the mythical hero [[Yamato Takeru]] during his campaign in eastern Japan in the 40th year of the reign of his father, [[Emperor Keikō]], to pray for the end of a drought that afflicted the area.{{cite web|title=About Oohi Jinja Shrine (Funabashi Daijingū Shrine)|url=http://oohijinja.jp/history-eng.html|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|accessdate=15 August 2017}}{{cite book |last1=Fujisawa |first1=Morihiko |title=日本伝説叢書 下総の巻 (Nihon Densetsu Sōsho: Shimōsa no Maki) |date=1919 |publisher=Nihon Densetsu Sōsho Kankōkai |pages=85–87 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/953575/62}}{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=259–261 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社 (Ōhi-jinja)|url=http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=%5E$&search:word=3061|access-date=2020-11-24|website=神社のひろば 神社探検隊！|publisher=Chiba Jinjachō}} The shrine first appears in the historical record as "Ōhi-no-Kami (意富比神) of [[Shimōsa Province]]" in the ''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (901), which records its promotion to higher [[List of Japanese court ranks, positions and hereditary titles|ranks]] ([[:ja:神階|神階]], ''shinkai'') by the imperial court in the mid-9th century, starting from 863 ([[Jōgan]] 5) when it was raised from the rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) to senior fifth, lower grade (正五位下). It was promoted again in 871 (Jōgan 13) to senior fifth rank, upper grade (正五位上), and finally in 874 (Jōgan 16) to junior fourth, lower grade (従四位下).{{cite web |title=日本三代實録 (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku) |website=J-TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館 |accessdate=2020-11-21 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519144319/http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html|url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html |archivedate=2018-05-19 |language=Japanese}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社（下総国葛飾郡）|url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/190201.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=Shinto Jinja Database|publisher=Kokugakuin University|language=Japanese}} It is listed as a "minor shrine" (小社, ''shōsha'') in the ''Jinmyōchō'' ("Register of Deities") section of the ''[[Engishiki]]'' (927 CE).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社|url=http://engishiki.org/shimousa/bun/smf200702-01.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=延喜式神社の調査}} While the shrine is currently dedicated to the imperial sun goddess [[Amaterasu]], one theory suggests that it may have originally venerated a local [[solar deity]] (the name ''Ōhi'' may be interpreted as meaning "great sun") who became conflated with Amaterasu during the medieval era. [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi]] and his son [[Minamoto no Yoshiie|Yoshiie]] is said to have rebuilt the shrine somewhere during the [[Tengi|Tengi era]] (1053-1058). In 1138 ([[Hōen]] 4), the area in which the shrine was located became a tribute estate or ''mikuriya'' (御厨) of the [[Grand Shrine of Ise]] known as 'Natsumi Mikuriya' (夏見御厨). The shrine became widely known as 'Funabashi Shinmei' (船橋神明) or 'Funabashi Ise Daijingū' (船橋伊勢大神宮) from the medieval period onwards, suggesting that the [[Shinto shrine#Famous shrines and shrine networks|branch]] of Ise Shrine (神明社, ''shinmeisha'') established within the estate was merged with it at some point. [[File:舩橋意富比神社 - Ōhi Shrine (Funabashi).jpg|thumb|left|430x430px|Ōhi Shrine during the [[Edo period]] (from the ''[[Edo meisho zue]]'')]][[Nichiren]], the founder of [[Nichiren Buddhism]], is said to have performed a ritual [[Fasting|fast]] at the shrine and offered a [[Gohonzon]] and a sword to it.{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=270–273 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}} At the beginning of the [[Edo period]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]] donated land worth fifty ''[[koku]]'' to the shrine. He is also said to have presented a wooden statue of Yamato Takeru to it in 1608 (Keichō 13). The statue was installed by Ieyasu's son and successor, [[Tokugawa Hidetada|Hidetada]], in a newly-constructed [[Setsumatsusha|auxiliary shrine]] in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8), in which he also enshrined [[Tōshō-gū|the deified spirit]] of his late father. Hidetada himself would later be enshrined there by his son [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]], the third ''[[shōgun]]'' of the [[Tokugawa shogunate|Tokugawa dynasty]].{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=262–263}} The shrine was destroyed during the [[:ja:市川・船橋戦争|Battle of Funabashi]] (part of the [[Boshin War]]) in 1868 ([[Keiō]] 4).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=灯明台|url=https://www.city.funabashi.lg.jp/kurashi/gakushu/0005/p008848.html|access-date=2020-11-23|website=Funabashi City Official Website|language=Japanese}} The main sanctuary (''[[honden]]'') was rebuilt in 1873 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] 6), with the ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' and other shrine buildings being rebuilt in 1923 ([[Taishō]] 12), 1963 ([[Shōwa (1926–1989)|Shōwa]] 38), 1975 (Shōwa 50), and 1985 (Shōwa 60), respectively. ==Structures== === Auxiliary shrines === The shrine contains a number of auxiliary shrines (''[[setsumatsusha]]'') within its precincts, some of which are: *'''Toyoukehime Shrine (豊受姫神社, ''Toyoukehime-jinja''), a.k.a. ''Gekū'' (外宮)''' :An auxiliary shrine dedicated to [[Toyoukebime|Toyoukehime]] (Toyouke-no-Ōkami), the goddess of the Outer Shrine (''Gekū'') of Ise. [[Historical kana orthography|historical orthography]]: ''Ohohi-jinja''), also known as '''Funabashi Daijingū''' (船橋大神宮), is a [[Shinto]] [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] dedicated to the [[Solar deity|sun goddess]] [[Amaterasu]] located in the city of [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]] in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. ==History== Legend claims that Ōhi Shrine was founded by the mythical hero [[Yamato Takeru]] during his campaign in eastern Japan in the 40th year of the reign of his father, [[Emperor Keikō]], to pray for the end of a drought that afflicted the area.{{cite web|title=About Oohi Jinja Shrine (Funabashi Daijingū Shrine)|url=http://oohijinja.jp/history-eng.html|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|accessdate=15 August 2017}}{{cite book |last1=Fujisawa |first1=Morihiko |title=日本伝説叢書 下総の巻 (Nihon Densetsu Sōsho: Shimōsa no Maki) |date=1919 |publisher=Nihon Densetsu Sōsho Kankōkai |pages=85–87 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/953575/62}}{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=259–261 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社 (Ōhi-jinja)|url=http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=%5E$&search:word=3061|access-date=2020-11-24|website=神社のひろば 神社探検隊！|publisher=Chiba Jinjachō}} The shrine first appears in the historical record as "Ōhi-no-Kami (意富比神) of [[Shimōsa Province]]" in the ''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (901), which records its promotion to higher [[List of Japanese court ranks, positions and hereditary titles|ranks]] ([[:ja:神階|神階]], ''shinkai'') by the imperial court in the mid-9th century, starting from 863 ([[Jōgan]] 5) when it was raised from the rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) to senior fifth, lower grade (正五位下). It was promoted again in 871 (Jōgan 13) to senior fifth rank, upper grade (正五位上), and finally in 874 (Jōgan 16) to junior fourth, lower grade (従四位下).{{cite web |title=日本三代實録 (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku) |website=J-TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館 |accessdate=2020-11-21 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519144319/http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html|url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html |archivedate=2018-05-19 |language=Japanese}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社（下総国葛飾郡）|url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/190201.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=Shinto Jinja Database|publisher=Kokugakuin University|language=Japanese}} It is listed as a "minor shrine" (小社, ''shōsha'') in the ''Jinmyōchō'' ("Register of Deities") section of the ''[[Engishiki]]'' (927 CE).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社|url=http://engishiki.org/shimousa/bun/smf200702-01.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=延喜式神社の調査}} While the shrine is currently dedicated to the imperial sun goddess [[Amaterasu]], one theory suggests that it may have originally venerated a local [[solar deity]] (the name ''Ōhi'' may be interpreted as meaning "great sun") who became conflated with Amaterasu during the medieval era. [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi]] and his son [[Minamoto no Yoshiie|Yoshiie]] is said to have rebuilt the shrine somewhere during the [[Tengi|Tengi era]] (1053-1058). In 1138 ([[Hōen]] 4), the area in which the shrine was located became a tribute estate or ''mikuriya'' (御厨) of the [[Grand Shrine of Ise]] known as 'Natsumi Mikuriya' (夏見御厨). The shrine became widely known as 'Funabashi Shinmei' (船橋神明) or 'Funabashi Ise Daijingū' (船橋伊勢大神宮) from the medieval period onwards, suggesting that the [[Shinto shrine#Famous shrines and shrine networks|branch]] of Ise Shrine (神明社, ''shinmeisha'') established within the estate was merged with it at some point. [[File:舩橋意富比神社 - Ōhi Shrine (Funabashi).jpg|thumb|left|430x430px|Ōhi Shrine during the [[Edo period]] (from the ''[[Edo meisho zue]]'')]][[Nichiren]], the founder of [[Nichiren Buddhism]], is said to have performed a ritual [[Fasting|fast]] at the shrine and offered a [[Gohonzon]] and a sword to it.{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=270–273 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}} At the beginning of the [[Edo period]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]] donated land worth fifty ''[[koku]]'' to the shrine. He is also said to have presented a wooden statue of Yamato Takeru to it in 1608 (Keichō 13). The statue was installed by Ieyasu's son and successor, [[Tokugawa Hidetada|Hidetada]], in a newly-constructed [[Setsumatsusha|auxiliary shrine]] in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8), in which he also enshrined [[Tōshō-gū|the deified spirit]] of his late father. Hidetada himself would later be enshrined there by his son [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]], the third ''[[shōgun]]'' of the [[Tokugawa shogunate|Tokugawa dynasty]].{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=262–263}} The shrine was destroyed during the [[:ja:市川・船橋戦争|Battle of Funabashi]] (part of the [[Boshin War]]) in 1868 ([[Keiō]] 4).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=灯明台|url=https://www.city.funabashi.lg.jp/kurashi/gakushu/0005/p008848.html|access-date=2020-11-23|website=Funabashi City Official Website|language=Japanese}} The main sanctuary (''[[honden]]'') was rebuilt in 1873 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] 6), with the ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' and other shrine buildings being rebuilt in 1923 ([[Taishō]] 12), 1963 ([[Shōwa (1926–1989)|Shōwa]] 38), 1975 (Shōwa 50), and 1985 (Shōwa 60), respectively. ==Structures== === Auxiliary shrines === The shrine contains a number of auxiliary shrines (''[[setsumatsusha]]'') within its precincts, some of which are: *'''Toyoukehime Shrine (豊受姫神社, ''Toyoukehime-jinja''), a.k.a. ''Gekū'' (外宮)''' :An auxiliary shrine dedicated to [[Toyoukebime|Toyoukehime]] (Toyouke-no-Ōkami), the goddess of the Outer Shrine (''Gekū'') of Ise. The shrine was renovated in 2015 using wood formerly used in the Inner Ise Shrine (''Naikū'').{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=豊受姫神社（外宮）竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/toyoukehimejinja-gaigu-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''Tokiwa Shrine (常盤神社)''' :Dedicated to [[Yamato Takeru]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]], and [[Tokugawa Hidetada]]. Originally established by Hidetada in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8) to enshrine Yamato Takeru and his father Ieyasu, he was also eventually enshrined alongside them as a deity by his son and successor [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]]. The current shrine building, replacing the previous one constructed during the Meiji period, was built in 2015 to commemorate the upcoming 400th anniversary of Ieyasu's death the following year.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=常磐神社竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/tokiwajinja-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2015-12-07|title=意富比神社（船橋大神宮）|url=https://jinja.tokyolovers.jp/chiba/funabashi/oohijinja|access-date=2020-11-27|website=神社と御朱印|language=ja}} *'''Yakumo Shrine (八雲神社, ''Yakumo-jinja'')''' :This shrine, located beside the ''Gekū'', enshrines [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]], [[Kushinadahime]], and [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi]] (Ōkuninushi). * '''Ōtori Shrine (大鳥神社, ''Ōtori-jinja'')''' :Dedicated to Yamato Takeru. *'''Ame-no-Mihashira Shrine (天之御柱宮, ''Ame-no-Mihashira-no-miya'')''' :Dedicated to the ''eirei'' (英霊, "heroic spirits") or war dead who lost their lives in service of Japan. *'''Yatsurugi Shrine (八劔神社, ''Yatsurugi-jinja'') and [[Yasaka Shrine]] (八坂神社, ''Yasaka-jinja'')''' :The two shrines, both dedicated to Susanoo, are in the form of two ''[[mikoshi]]'' housed within a single building.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=境内のご案内|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/guide/|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''[[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Shrine]] (金刀比羅社, ''Kotohira-sha'')''' *'''Funatama Shrine (船玉神社)''' :This boat-shaped shrine is currently dedicated to [[Kamiumi|Ame-no-Torifune]] and the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha|Sumiyoshi deities]], though the shrine's name suggests it may have originally venerated the ''[[:ja:船霊|funadama]]'' ("boat spirit"), a folk deity worshiped by fishermen and sailors as a protector of ships.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Funadama|url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/bts/bts_f.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Basic Terms of 意富比神社 (船橋大神宮) | image = Oohi-jinja(Funabashi) Haiden.jpg | caption =The prayer area (''haisho'') before the shrine's ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|41|46.17|N|139|59|34.58|E|region:JP_type:landmark_scale:1000|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Amaterasu]] | founded_by = [[Yamato Takeru]] (legendary) | established = 40th year of the reign of [[Emperor Keikō]] (legendary) | date_destroyed = | location = 5-2-1, Miyamoto, [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]]
[[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]] 273-0003 | website = http://oohijinja.jp/index.html | architecture_style = ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' | festival = 20 October | leadership = }} '''Ōhi Shrine''' (意富比神社, ''Ōhi-jinja''; [[Historical kana orthography|historical orthography]]: ''Ohohi-jinja''), also known as '''Funabashi Daijingū''' (船橋大神宮), is a [[Shinto]] [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] dedicated to the [[Solar deity|sun goddess]] [[Amaterasu]] located in the city of [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]] in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. ==History== Legend claims that Ōhi Shrine was founded by the mythical hero [[Yamato Takeru]] during his campaign in eastern Japan in the 40th year of the reign of his father, [[Emperor Keikō]], to pray for the end of a drought that afflicted the area.{{cite web|title=About Oohi Jinja Shrine (Funabashi Daijingū Shrine)|url=http://oohijinja.jp/history-eng.html|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|accessdate=15 August 2017}}{{cite book |last1=Fujisawa |first1=Morihiko |title=日本伝説叢書 下総の巻 (Nihon Densetsu Sōsho: Shimōsa no Maki) |date=1919 |publisher=Nihon Densetsu Sōsho Kankōkai |pages=85–87 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/953575/62}}{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=259–261 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社 (Ōhi-jinja)|url=http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=%5E$&search:word=3061|access-date=2020-11-24|website=神社のひろば 神社探検隊！|publisher=Chiba Jinjachō}} The shrine first appears in the historical record as "Ōhi-no-Kami (意富比神) of [[Shimōsa Province]]" in the ''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (901), which records its promotion to higher [[List of Japanese court ranks, positions and hereditary titles|ranks]] ([[:ja:神階|神階]], ''shinkai'') by the imperial court in the mid-9th century, starting from 863 ([[Jōgan]] 5) when it was raised from the rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) to senior fifth, lower grade (正五位下). It was promoted again in 871 (Jōgan 13) to senior fifth rank, upper grade (正五位上), and finally in 874 (Jōgan 16) to junior fourth, lower grade (従四位下).{{cite web |title=日本三代實録 (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku) |website=J-TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館 |accessdate=2020-11-21 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519144319/http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html|url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html |archivedate=2018-05-19 |language=Japanese}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社（下総国葛飾郡）|url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/190201.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=Shinto Jinja Database|publisher=Kokugakuin University|language=Japanese}} It is listed as a "minor shrine" (小社, ''shōsha'') in the ''Jinmyōchō'' ("Register of Deities") section of the ''[[Engishiki]]'' (927 CE).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社|url=http://engishiki.org/shimousa/bun/smf200702-01.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=延喜式神社の調査}} While the shrine is currently dedicated to the imperial sun goddess [[Amaterasu]], one theory suggests that it may have originally venerated a local [[solar deity]] (the name ''Ōhi'' may be interpreted as meaning "great sun") who became conflated with Amaterasu during the medieval era. [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi]] and his son [[Minamoto no Yoshiie|Yoshiie]] is said to have rebuilt the shrine somewhere during the [[Tengi|Tengi era]] (1053-1058). In 1138 ([[Hōen]] 4), the area in which the shrine was located became a tribute estate or ''mikuriya'' (御厨) of the [[Grand Shrine of Ise]] known as 'Natsumi Mikuriya' (夏見御厨). The shrine became widely known as 'Funabashi Shinmei' (船橋神明) or 'Funabashi Ise Daijingū' (船橋伊勢大神宮) from the medieval period onwards, suggesting that the [[Shinto shrine#Famous shrines and shrine networks|branch]] of Ise Shrine (神明社, ''shinmeisha'') established within the estate was merged with it at some point. [[File:舩橋意富比神社 - Ōhi Shrine (Funabashi).jpg|thumb|left|430x430px|Ōhi Shrine during the [[Edo period]] (from the ''[[Edo meisho zue]]'')]][[Nichiren]], the founder of [[Nichiren Buddhism]], is said to have performed a ritual [[Fasting|fast]] at the shrine and offered a [[Gohonzon]] and a sword to it.{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=270–273 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}} At the beginning of the [[Edo period]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]] donated land worth fifty ''[[koku]]'' to the shrine. He is also said to have presented a wooden statue of Yamato Takeru to it in 1608 (Keichō 13). The statue was installed by Ieyasu's son and successor, [[Tokugawa Hidetada|Hidetada]], in a newly-constructed [[Setsumatsusha|auxiliary shrine]] in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8), in which he also enshrined [[Tōshō-gū|the deified spirit]] of his late father. Hidetada himself would later be enshrined there by his son [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]], the third ''[[shōgun]]'' of the [[Tokugawa shogunate|Tokugawa dynasty]].{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=262–263}} The shrine was destroyed during the [[:ja:市川・船橋戦争|Battle of Funabashi]] (part of the [[Boshin War]]) in 1868 ([[Keiō]] 4).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=灯明台|url=https://www.city.funabashi.lg.jp/kurashi/gakushu/0005/p008848.html|access-date=2020-11-23|website=Funabashi City Official Website|language=Japanese}} The main sanctuary (''[[honden]]'') was rebuilt in 1873 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] 6), with the ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' and other shrine buildings being rebuilt in 1923 ([[Taishō]] 12), 1963 ([[Shōwa (1926–1989)|Shōwa]] 38), 1975 (Shōwa 50), and 1985 (Shōwa 60), respectively. ==Structures== === Auxiliary shrines === The shrine contains a number of auxiliary shrines (''[[setsumatsusha]]'') within its precincts, some of which are: *'''Toyoukehime Shrine (豊受姫神社, ''Toyoukehime-jinja''), a.k.a. ''Gekū'' (外宮)''' :An auxiliary shrine dedicated to [[Toyoukebime|Toyoukehime]] (Toyouke-no-Ōkami), the goddess of the Outer Shrine (''Gekū'') of Ise. The shrine was renovated in 2015 using wood formerly used in the Inner Ise Shrine (''Naikū'').{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=豊受姫神社（外宮）竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/toyoukehimejinja-gaigu-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''Tokiwa Shrine (常盤神社)''' :Dedicated to [[Yamato Takeru]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]], and [[Tokugawa Hidetada]]. Originally established by Hidetada in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8) to enshrine Yamato Takeru and his father Ieyasu, he was also eventually enshrined alongside them as a deity by his son and successor [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]]. The current shrine building, replacing the previous one constructed during the Meiji period, was built in 2015 to commemorate the upcoming 400th anniversary of Ieyasu's death the following year.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=常磐神社竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/tokiwajinja-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2015-12-07|title=意富比神社（船橋大神宮）|url=https://jinja.tokyolovers.jp/chiba/funabashi/oohijinja|access-date=2020-11-27|website=神社と御朱印|language=ja}} *'''Yakumo Shrine (八雲神社, ''Yakumo-jinja'')''' :This shrine, located beside the ''Gekū'', enshrines [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]], [[Kushinadahime]], and [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi]] (Ōkuninushi). * '''Ōtori Shrine (大鳥神社, ''Ōtori-jinja'')''' :Dedicated to Yamato Takeru. *'''Ame-no-Mihashira Shrine (天之御柱宮, ''Ame-no-Mihashira-no-miya'')''' :Dedicated to the ''eirei'' (英霊, "heroic spirits") or war dead who lost their lives in service of Japan. *'''Yatsurugi Shrine (八劔神社, ''Yatsurugi-jinja'') and [[Yasaka Shrine]] (八坂神社, ''Yasaka-jinja'')''' :The two shrines, both dedicated to Susanoo, are in the form of two ''[[mikoshi]]'' housed within a single building.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=境内のご案内|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/guide/|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''[[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Shrine]] (金刀比羅社, ''Kotohira-sha'')''' *'''Funatama Shrine (船玉神社)''' :This boat-shaped shrine is currently dedicated to [[Kamiumi|Ame-no-Torifune]] and the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha|Sumiyoshi deities]], though the shrine's name suggests it may have originally venerated the ''[[:ja:船霊|funadama]]'' ("boat spirit"), a folk deity worshiped by fishermen and sailors as a protector of ships.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Funadama|url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/bts/bts_f.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Basic Terms of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University}} {|style="margin: 0 auto;" | [[File:Oohi-jinja(Funabashi) Ootori-jinja.jpg|thumb|Ōtori Shrine (大鳥神社)]] | [[File:Oohi-jinja(Funabashi) Funatama-jinja.jpg|thumb|Funatama Shrine (船玉神社)]] | [[File:Oohijinjya5.jpg|thumb|The exterior of Tokiwa Shrine before its 2015 renovation]] |} ==Festivals== {{Empty section|date=May 2021}} [[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]] 273-0003 | website = http://oohijinja.jp/index.html | architecture_style = ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' | festival = 20 October | leadership = }} '''Ōhi Shrine''' (意富比神社, ''Ōhi-jinja''; [[Historical kana orthography|historical orthography]]: ''Ohohi-jinja''), also known as '''Funabashi Daijingū''' (船橋大神宮), is a [[Shinto]] [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] dedicated to the [[Solar deity|sun goddess]] [[Amaterasu]] located in the city of [[Funabashi, Chiba|Funabashi]] in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. ==History== Legend claims that Ōhi Shrine was founded by the mythical hero [[Yamato Takeru]] during his campaign in eastern Japan in the 40th year of the reign of his father, [[Emperor Keikō]], to pray for the end of a drought that afflicted the area.{{cite web|title=About Oohi Jinja Shrine (Funabashi Daijingū Shrine)|url=http://oohijinja.jp/history-eng.html|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|accessdate=15 August 2017}}{{cite book |last1=Fujisawa |first1=Morihiko |title=日本伝説叢書 下総の巻 (Nihon Densetsu Sōsho: Shimōsa no Maki) |date=1919 |publisher=Nihon Densetsu Sōsho Kankōkai |pages=85–87 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/953575/62}}{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=259–261 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社 (Ōhi-jinja)|url=http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=%5E$&search:word=3061|access-date=2020-11-24|website=神社のひろば 神社探検隊！|publisher=Chiba Jinjachō}} The shrine first appears in the historical record as "Ōhi-no-Kami (意富比神) of [[Shimōsa Province]]" in the ''[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]'' (901), which records its promotion to higher [[List of Japanese court ranks, positions and hereditary titles|ranks]] ([[:ja:神階|神階]], ''shinkai'') by the imperial court in the mid-9th century, starting from 863 ([[Jōgan]] 5) when it was raised from the rank of junior fifth, lower grade (従五位下) to senior fifth, lower grade (正五位下). It was promoted again in 871 (Jōgan 13) to senior fifth rank, upper grade (正五位上), and finally in 874 (Jōgan 16) to junior fourth, lower grade (従四位下).{{cite web |title=日本三代實録 (Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku) |website=J-TEXTS 日本文学電子図書館 |accessdate=2020-11-21 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519144319/http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html|url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html |archivedate=2018-05-19 |language=Japanese}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社（下総国葛飾郡）|url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/190201.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=Shinto Jinja Database|publisher=Kokugakuin University|language=Japanese}} It is listed as a "minor shrine" (小社, ''shōsha'') in the ''Jinmyōchō'' ("Register of Deities") section of the ''[[Engishiki]]'' (927 CE).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=意富比神社|url=http://engishiki.org/shimousa/bun/smf200702-01.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=延喜式神社の調査}} While the shrine is currently dedicated to the imperial sun goddess [[Amaterasu]], one theory suggests that it may have originally venerated a local [[solar deity]] (the name ''Ōhi'' may be interpreted as meaning "great sun") who became conflated with Amaterasu during the medieval era. [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi]] and his son [[Minamoto no Yoshiie|Yoshiie]] is said to have rebuilt the shrine somewhere during the [[Tengi|Tengi era]] (1053-1058). In 1138 ([[Hōen]] 4), the area in which the shrine was located became a tribute estate or ''mikuriya'' (御厨) of the [[Grand Shrine of Ise]] known as 'Natsumi Mikuriya' (夏見御厨). The shrine became widely known as 'Funabashi Shinmei' (船橋神明) or 'Funabashi Ise Daijingū' (船橋伊勢大神宮) from the medieval period onwards, suggesting that the [[Shinto shrine#Famous shrines and shrine networks|branch]] of Ise Shrine (神明社, ''shinmeisha'') established within the estate was merged with it at some point. [[File:舩橋意富比神社 - Ōhi Shrine (Funabashi).jpg|thumb|left|430x430px|Ōhi Shrine during the [[Edo period]] (from the ''[[Edo meisho zue]]'')]][[Nichiren]], the founder of [[Nichiren Buddhism]], is said to have performed a ritual [[Fasting|fast]] at the shrine and offered a [[Gohonzon]] and a sword to it.{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=270–273 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FivRe73ZVU8C}} At the beginning of the [[Edo period]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]] donated land worth fifty ''[[koku]]'' to the shrine. He is also said to have presented a wooden statue of Yamato Takeru to it in 1608 (Keichō 13). The statue was installed by Ieyasu's son and successor, [[Tokugawa Hidetada|Hidetada]], in a newly-constructed [[Setsumatsusha|auxiliary shrine]] in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8), in which he also enshrined [[Tōshō-gū|the deified spirit]] of his late father. Hidetada himself would later be enshrined there by his son [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]], the third ''[[shōgun]]'' of the [[Tokugawa shogunate|Tokugawa dynasty]].{{cite book |editor=Chiba-ken Higashi-Katsushika-gun Funabashi-machi |title=船橋町誌 (Funabashi-machi Shi) |date=1937 |publisher=Keiseisha |pages=262–263}} The shrine was destroyed during the [[:ja:市川・船橋戦争|Battle of Funabashi]] (part of the [[Boshin War]]) in 1868 ([[Keiō]] 4).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=灯明台|url=https://www.city.funabashi.lg.jp/kurashi/gakushu/0005/p008848.html|access-date=2020-11-23|website=Funabashi City Official Website|language=Japanese}} The main sanctuary (''[[honden]]'') was rebuilt in 1873 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] 6), with the ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' and other shrine buildings being rebuilt in 1923 ([[Taishō]] 12), 1963 ([[Shōwa (1926–1989)|Shōwa]] 38), 1975 (Shōwa 50), and 1985 (Shōwa 60), respectively. ==Structures== === Auxiliary shrines === The shrine contains a number of auxiliary shrines (''[[setsumatsusha]]'') within its precincts, some of which are: *'''Toyoukehime Shrine (豊受姫神社, ''Toyoukehime-jinja''), a.k.a. ''Gekū'' (外宮)''' :An auxiliary shrine dedicated to [[Toyoukebime|Toyoukehime]] (Toyouke-no-Ōkami), the goddess of the Outer Shrine (''Gekū'') of Ise. The shrine was renovated in 2015 using wood formerly used in the Inner Ise Shrine (''Naikū'').{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=豊受姫神社（外宮）竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/toyoukehimejinja-gaigu-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''Tokiwa Shrine (常盤神社)''' :Dedicated to [[Yamato Takeru]], [[Tokugawa Ieyasu]], and [[Tokugawa Hidetada]]. Originally established by Hidetada in 1622 ([[Genna]] 8) to enshrine Yamato Takeru and his father Ieyasu, he was also eventually enshrined alongside them as a deity by his son and successor [[Tokugawa Iemitsu|Iemitsu]]. The current shrine building, replacing the previous one constructed during the Meiji period, was built in 2015 to commemorate the upcoming 400th anniversary of Ieyasu's death the following year.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=常磐神社竣工のお知らせ|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/news/2015/tokiwajinja-shunko.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}}{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2015-12-07|title=意富比神社（船橋大神宮）|url=https://jinja.tokyolovers.jp/chiba/funabashi/oohijinja|access-date=2020-11-27|website=神社と御朱印|language=ja}} *'''Yakumo Shrine (八雲神社, ''Yakumo-jinja'')''' :This shrine, located beside the ''Gekū'', enshrines [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]], [[Kushinadahime]], and [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi]] (Ōkuninushi). * '''Ōtori Shrine (大鳥神社, ''Ōtori-jinja'')''' :Dedicated to Yamato Takeru. *'''Ame-no-Mihashira Shrine (天之御柱宮, ''Ame-no-Mihashira-no-miya'')''' :Dedicated to the ''eirei'' (英霊, "heroic spirits") or war dead who lost their lives in service of Japan. *'''Yatsurugi Shrine (八劔神社, ''Yatsurugi-jinja'') and [[Yasaka Shrine]] (八坂神社, ''Yasaka-jinja'')''' :The two shrines, both dedicated to Susanoo, are in the form of two ''[[mikoshi]]'' housed within a single building.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=境内のご案内|url=http://www.oohijinja.jp/guide/|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Ōhi Shrine Official Website|language=ja-JP}} *'''[[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Shrine]] (金刀比羅社, ''Kotohira-sha'')''' *'''Funatama Shrine (船玉神社)''' :This boat-shaped shrine is currently dedicated to [[Kamiumi|Ame-no-Torifune]] and the [[Sumiyoshi-taisha|Sumiyoshi deities]], though the shrine's name suggests it may have originally venerated the ''[[:ja:船霊|funadama]]'' ("boat spirit"), a folk deity worshiped by fishermen and sailors as a protector of ships.{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Funadama|url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/bts/bts_f.html|access-date=2020-11-27|website=Basic Terms of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University}} {|style="margin: 0 auto;" | [[File:Oohi-jinja(Funabashi) Ootori-jinja.jpg|thumb|Ōtori Shrine (大鳥神社)]] | [[File:Oohi-jinja(Funabashi) Funatama-jinja.jpg|thumb|Funatama Shrine (船玉神社)]] | [[File:Oohijinjya5.jpg|thumb|The exterior of Tokiwa Shrine before its 2015 renovation]] |} ==Festivals== {{Empty section|date=May 2021}}
