Its common name is ``Funabashi Daijingu'' (Funabashi Daijingu). In the Engishiki ceremony, it appears under the name ``Katsugo-gun Ifuhi Shrine.'' === Enshrined God === * '''{{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|1=Amaterasu}}''' ===Origin of company name=== There are various theories about the origin of the company's name, ``Ohhi, {{ill|lt=Historical kana usage|UNKNOWN|lt=Old kana usage}}: Ohohi. The main ones are shown below. * The theory that he is a food god, meaning a great fire or a great meal. * The theory is that it is a sunset because it is located on a hill that is directly facing the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sunset|1=UNKNOWN}} sun. * Theory that the {{ill|lt=guardian deity|Q767655|WD=Q767655|1=Ujigami}} of the {{ill|lt=Ta clan|Q11430816|WD=Q11430816|lt=Yitomi|1=Ō clan}}, an ancient and powerful ruling family. * This theory, which means Dainichi, is Otendo-sama (sun god), which {{ill|lt=farmers|Q838811|WD=Q838811|1=Peasant}} in this region had originally worshiped.{{efn|This theory was announced as a theory that added criticism and research to the previous theories, and attracted attention. As if to support this theory, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tendo Nenbutsu|1=UNKNOWN}} has been popular in the city since ancient times, and Daijingu Shrine also has a hanging Buddha statue representing the ``Dainichi Nyorai statue'' that was used before the {{ill|lt=Separation of Shinto and Buddhism|Shinto Buddhism Order|WD=Shinto Buddhism Order|ltq=Q1970535}} order was issued. }} === History === According to the shrine's legend, it began in the year 40 of {{ill|lt=Emperor Keiko|Q329723|WD=Q329723|1=Emperor Keikō}}, when {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru|1=UNKNOWN}} prayed for the pacification of the eastern region during his expedition to the east. At that time, the local residents were suffering from drought, and when Nihon Takeru prayed for rain at the same time, it was said that it started raining. Originally, the local sun god ``Itobijin (Dainichijin)'' was enshrined at the company, and it attracted the faith of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=fishermen|1=UNKNOWN}} in the surrounding area ({{ill|lt=Tokyo Bay|Q141017|WD=Q141017|1=Tokyo Bay}}). The first time I read {{ill|lt=Rokukokushi|Q1151168|WD=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi|1=Rikkokushi}} is in "{{ill|lt=Jihon Sandai Joroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}" (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōkan}}5 years ({{ill|lt=863 years|Q25052|WD=Q25052|1=863}}) In the article dated May 26, {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, it is listed as a small shrine.Later, this area was donated to {{ill|lt=Ise Jingu|Q687168|WD=Q687168|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} and {{ill|lt=Mikuriya|Q11488831|WD=Q11488831|1=mikuriya}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Natsumi Mikuriya|1=UNKNOWN}}), and Shinmeisha Shrine, which enshrines Amaterasu Omikami, the deity of Ise Grand Shrine, as its guardian, is now {{jalink|Hie Shrine} in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Natsumidai|1=UNKNOWN}}. (Natsumidai, Funabashi City) ||Hie Shrine}} However, with the decline of Mikuriya, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinmeisha|1=UNKNOWN}} also became obsolete and was enshrined at Ifuhi Shrine. After that, faith in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu no Omikami|1=UNKNOWN}} became stronger, and the name of Ifuhi Shrine was gradually forgotten, and it came to be called exclusively Funabashi Shinmei or Funabashi Daijingu. Until the Sengoku period, the powerful {{ill|lt=Chiba clan|Q2975237|WD=Q2975237|1=Chiba clan}} family {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tomi clan|1=UNKNOWN}}, who maintained power in this area, served as {{ill|lt=chief priest|Q11453500|WD=Q11453500|1=Gūji}}. Even now, he has changed his surname to Chiba, and members of the same family serve as {{ill|lt=chief priest|Q11453500|WD=Q11453500|1=Gūji}}. The shrine held many medieval documents, including the {{jalink|Ichikawa-Funabashi War|Q812} from the Boshin War that occurred during the {{ill|lt=Meiji Restoration|Q8707|WD=Q8707|1=Meiji Restoration}}. 56|Battle of Funabashi}} It was burnt down along with the shrine building, and only a few items remain today, including letters from Mitsutane Chiba and a document dating back many years called ``Funabashi Mikuriya Rokuga Goda Kazunoji.'' The main hall was rebuilt in 1896, and the worship hall was rebuilt in 1891. In 1872, it was elevated to the status of a prefectural shrine, and the name was restored to Ifuhi Shrine as recorded in the Engishiki Shinmyocho.It was revered by the imperial court and the shogunate, and members such as {{ill|lt=Taira no Masakado|Q1207652|WD=Q1207652|1=Taira no Masakado}}, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, and {{ill|lt=Ieyasu Tokugawa|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}} donated shrine territories and built and renovated the shrine buildings. At Tokiwa Shrine in the grounds of the shrine, a wooden Ieyasu statue containing Ieyasu's tooth is enshrined. In modern times, successive emperors such as {{ill|lt=Emperor Meiji|Q174231|WD=Q174231|1=Emperor Meiji}}, {{ill|lt=Emperor Taisho|Q157052|WD=Q157052|1=Emperor Taishō}}, and {{ill|lt=Emperor Showa|Q34479|WD=Q34479|1=Hirohito}} have visited the shrine. === Rank salary === * {{ill|lt=863 years|Q25052|WD=Q25052|1=863}} (Jōkan 5th year) {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} confers {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Seigoi Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} * {{ill|lt=871|Q24754|WD=Q24754|1=871}} (13th year of Jogan) {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Senior Fifth Rank Upper|1=UNKNOWN}} awarded * {{ill|lt=874|Q23843|WD=Q23843|1=874}} (16th year of Jogan) Awarded {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} {{efn|{{ill|lt=Nara period|Q189178|WD=Q189178|1=Nara period}}, systems regarding {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Jingi|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=rituals|1=UNKNOWN}} were put in place, and he began to receive generous protection from the Ritsuryo state. Also, from this time the custom (shakaku) of conferring official rank on gods (shrines) arose. According to records, Honsha was awarded the rank of 4th rank in the 16th year of the Jogan era. This effectively means that he was ranked higher than the fifth rank, which was appointed as {{ill|lt=Shimosa Province|Q1053695|WD=Q1053695|1=Shimōsa Province}}{{ill|lt=Kokushi|Q1351234|WD=Q1351234|1=Kokushi (official)}}, and shows that the head office was positioned as an important shrine at that time. However, there is no clear reason why he was given such a high rank. However, it is generally believed that they were trying to increase the influence of {{ill|lt=Yamato Dynasty|Q2658252|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Dynasty|1=Yamato Kingship}} by bestowing a high rank on the headquarters, which was highly worshiped by the residents of this region. }} {{Right|[[Image:tomeidaiⅱ.jpg|thumb|none|Lighthouse distant view]]}} === Precincts === === Setsusha === * '''Tokiwa Shrine'' (Setsusha) :{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}, and {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Hidetada|Q314464|WD=Q314464|lt=Tokugawa Hidetada|1=Tokugawa Hidetada}} are enshrined as deities. * '''{{ill|lt=Toyouke Daijingu|Q11633343|WD=Q11633343|lt=Geku|1=Toyōke Daijingū}}''' (Setsusha) :The enshrined deity is {{ill|lt=Toyoukebime|Q2983724|WD=Q2983724|lt=Toyoukehime Okami|1=Toyouke-hime}}. * '''{{ill|lt=Yakumo Shrine|Q11391847|WD=Q11391847|1=Yakumo shrine}}''' (Setsusha) :{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Susanoo no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} is the main deity, and {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Omi Takakami|1=Ōkuninushi}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kikiinada Hime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} are enshrined. * '''Ama no Onbashira Shrine'' (sub-sha) :Enshrines the {{ill|lt=Heroic Spirit|Q11617005|WD=Q11617005|1=eirei}} of the protector of the country. * '''Otori Shrine'' (Setsusha) :The enshrined deity is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru|1=UNKNOWN}}. * '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yatsurugi Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}・{{ill|lt=Yasaka Shrine|Q692714|WD=Q692714|1=Yasaka Shrine}}''' (Setsusha) :The enshrined deity is Susanoo no Mikoto and is enshrined in {{ill|lt=Mikoshi|Q979940|WD=Q979940|1=Mikoshi}}. * '''Funatama Shrine'' (sub-shrine) :{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amantorifune Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sankami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi Mikoto|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}} are the enshrined deities. It is enshrined on a hill in the northern part of the precincts. === Cultural assets === === Prefectural designated cultural property === * {{ill|lt=Funabashi Daijingu Lighthouse|Q11614129|WD=Q11614129|1=Funabashi Daijingū Tōmyōdai}} ({{ill|lt=List of Chiba Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties #Tangible Folk Cultural Properties|Q11406175|WD=Q11406175|lt=Chiba Prefecture Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties|1=Chiba Prefecture Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties}}) === City designated cultural property === * {{ill|lt=Kagura|Q1348260|WD=Q1348260|1=Kagura}} (City-designated intangible folk cultural property) === Event === === Dedicated Sumo at Funabashi Daijingu Shrine (October 20th) === The votive {{ill|lt=sumo|Q40561|WD=Q40561|1=Sumo}} held as an annual autumn festival has a long history, originating from {{ill|lt=Ieyasu Tokugawa|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}'s Kanran sumo held in {{ill|lt=1590|Q6764|WD=Q6764|1=1590}} ({{ill|lt=Tensho|Q1145058|WD=Q1145058|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)}}18). At that time, Ieyasu occasionally held falconry events in Shimousa, and had an annex set up as a lodging in {{ill|lt=Funabashi City|Q271417|WD=Q271417|lt=Funabashi|1=Funabashi}}. ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Funabashi Goten|1=UNKNOWN}} was located in what is now {{ill|lt=Funabashi City|Q271417|WD=Q271417|1=Funabashi}} Honmachi 4-chome, and was called "Gotenji." The former site is {{ill|lt=Funabashi Toshogu|Q11614238|WD=Q11614238|1=Funabashi-tōshōgū}}) One day, Ieyasu saw a child playing sumo. It is said that the origin of sumo is said to have been dedicated to Funabashi Daijingu Shrine, where people were deeply religious, and later on, {{ill|lt=Kanjin|Q6363447|WD=Q6363447|1=Kanjin}} himself became the origin of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=amateur sumo|1=UNKNOWN}}.Amateur sumo in Jingu is known for attracting strong wrestlers, and it still contributes to the training of {{ill|lt=sumo wrestlers|Q2727289|WD=Q2727289|1=Rikishi}} from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokatsu|1=UNKNOWN}}. {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=270|coord={{coord|35|41|46.4|N|139|59|34.7|E}}}} |Location={{ill|lt=Chiba Prefecture|Q80011|WD=Q80011|1=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Funabashi City|Q271417|WD=Q271417|1=Funabashi}}{{ill|lt=Miyamoto (Funabashi City)|Q24867638|WD=Q24867638|lt=Miyamoto|1=Miyamoto}}5-2-1 | Latitude degrees = 35 | Latitude minutes = 41 | Latitude seconds = 46.4 | N (northern latitude) and S (southern latitude) = N | Longitude degrees = 139 | Longitude minutes = 59 | Longitude seconds = 34.7 | E(East longitude) and W(West longitude) = E |Enshrined God={{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|1=Amaterasu}} |Company rank={{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}} (small)/{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural company|1=Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha}} |Main shrine={{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|WD=Q930545|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} |Founded={{ill|lt=Emperor Keiko|Q329723|WD=Q329723|1=Emperor Keikō}}40 years{{sfn|Edo Famous Places Encyclopedia|1927|p=371}} |Regular Festival={{ill|lt=October 20th|Q2959|WD=Q2959|1=October 20}} |Also known as Funabashi Daijingu Shrine |Map country code=JP |Map=Japan Chiba }}'''Ohijinja Shrine'' is located in {{ill|lt=Chiba Prefecture|Q80011|WD=Q80011|1=Chiba Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Funabashi City|Q271417|WD=Q271417|1=Funabashi}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}}, and the former {{ill|lt=shakaku|Q10444029|WD=Q10444029|1=Shakaku}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kensha|1=Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226}}. Its common name is ``Funabashi Daijingu'' (Funabashi Daijingu). In the Engishiki ceremony, it appears under the name ``Katsugo-gun Ifuhi Shrine.'' === Enshrined God === * '''{{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|1=Amaterasu}}''' ===Origin of company name=== There are various theories about the origin of the company's name, ``Ohhi, {{ill|lt=Historical kana usage|UNKNOWN|lt=Old kana usage}}: Ohohi. The main ones are shown below. * The theory that he is a food god, meaning a great fire or a great meal. * The theory is that it is a sunset because it is located on a hill that is directly facing the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sunset|1=UNKNOWN}} sun. * Theory that the {{ill|lt=guardian deity|Q767655|WD=Q767655|1=Ujigami}} of the {{ill|lt=Ta clan|Q11430816|WD=Q11430816|lt=Yitomi|1=Ō clan}}, an ancient and powerful ruling family. * This theory, which means Dainichi, is Otendo-sama (sun god), which {{ill|lt=farmers|Q838811|WD=Q838811|1=Peasant}} in this region had originally worshiped.{{efn|This theory was announced as a theory that added criticism and research to the previous theories, and attracted attention. As if to support this theory, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tendo Nenbutsu|1=UNKNOWN}} has been popular in the city since ancient times, and Daijingu Shrine also has a hanging Buddha statue representing the ``Dainichi Nyorai statue'' that was used before the {{ill|lt=Separation of Shinto and Buddhism|Shinto Buddhism Order|WD=Shinto Buddhism Order|ltq=Q1970535}} order was issued. }} === History === According to the shrine's legend, it began in the year 40 of {{ill|lt=Emperor Keiko|Q329723|WD=Q329723|1=Emperor Keikō}}, when {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru|1=UNKNOWN}} prayed for the pacification of the eastern region during his expedition to the east. At that time, the local residents were suffering from drought, and when Nihon Takeru prayed for rain at the same time, it was said that it started raining. Originally, the local sun god ``Itobijin (Dainichijin)'' was enshrined at the company, and it attracted the faith of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=fishermen|1=UNKNOWN}} in the surrounding area ({{ill|lt=Tokyo Bay|Q141017|WD=Q141017|1=Tokyo Bay}}). The first time I read {{ill|lt=Rokukokushi|Q1151168|WD=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi|1=Rikkokushi}} is in "{{ill|lt=Jihon Sandai Joroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}" (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōkan}}5 years ({{ill|lt=863 years|Q25052|WD=Q25052|1=863}}) In the article dated May 26, {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, it is listed as a small shrine.Later, this area was donated to {{ill|lt=Ise Jingu|Q687168|WD=Q687168|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} and {{ill|lt=Mikuriya|Q11488831|WD=Q11488831|1=mikuriya}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Natsumi Mikuriya|1=UNKNOWN}}), and Shinmeisha Shrine, which enshrines Amaterasu Omikami, the deity of Ise Grand Shrine, as its guardian, is now {{jalink|Hie Shrine} in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Natsumidai|1=UNKNOWN}}. (Natsumidai, Funabashi City) ||Hie Shrine}} However, with the decline of Mikuriya, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinmeisha|1=UNKNOWN}} also became obsolete and was enshrined at Ifuhi Shrine. After that, faith in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu no Omikami|1=UNKNOWN}} became stronger, and the name of Ifuhi Shrine was gradually forgotten, and it came to be called exclusively Funabashi Shinmei or Funabashi Daijingu. Until the Sengoku period, the powerful {{ill|lt=Chiba clan|Q2975237|WD=Q2975237|1=Chiba clan}} family {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tomi clan|1=UNKNOWN}}, who maintained power in this area, served as {{ill|lt=chief priest|Q11453500|WD=Q11453500|1=Gūji}}. Even now, he has changed his surname to Chiba, and members of the same family serve as {{ill|lt=chief priest|Q11453500|WD=Q11453500|1=Gūji}}. The shrine held many medieval documents, including the {{jalink|Ichikawa-Funabashi War|Q812} from the Boshin War that occurred during the {{ill|lt=Meiji Restoration|Q8707|WD=Q8707|1=Meiji Restoration}}. 56|Battle of Funabashi}} It was burnt down along with the shrine building, and only a few items remain today, including letters from Mitsutane Chiba and a document dating back many years called ``Funabashi Mikuriya Rokuga Goda Kazunoji.'' The main hall was rebuilt in 1896, and the worship hall was rebuilt in 1891. In 1872, it was elevated to the status of a prefectural shrine, and the name was restored to Ifuhi Shrine as recorded in the Engishiki Shinmyocho.It was revered by the imperial court and the shogunate, and members such as {{ill|lt=Taira no Masakado|Q1207652|WD=Q1207652|1=Taira no Masakado}}, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, and {{ill|lt=Ieyasu Tokugawa|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}} donated shrine territories and built and renovated the shrine buildings. At Tokiwa Shrine in the grounds of the shrine, a wooden Ieyasu statue containing Ieyasu's tooth is enshrined. In modern times, successive emperors such as {{ill|lt=Emperor Meiji|Q174231|WD=Q174231|1=Emperor Meiji}}, {{ill|lt=Emperor Taisho|Q157052|WD=Q157052|1=Emperor Taishō}}, and {{ill|lt=Emperor Showa|Q34479|WD=Q34479|1=Hirohito}} have visited the shrine. === Rank salary === * {{ill|lt=863 years|Q25052|WD=Q25052|1=863}} (Jōkan 5th year) {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} confers {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Seigoi Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} * {{ill|lt=871|Q24754|WD=Q24754|1=871}} (13th year of Jogan) {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Senior Fifth Rank Upper|1=UNKNOWN}} awarded * {{ill|lt=874|Q23843|WD=Q23843|1=874}} (16th year of Jogan) Awarded {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} {{efn|{{ill|lt=Nara period|Q189178|WD=Q189178|1=Nara period}}, systems regarding {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Jingi|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=rituals|1=UNKNOWN}} were put in place, and he began to receive generous protection from the Ritsuryo state. Also, from this time the custom (shakaku) of conferring official rank on gods (shrines) arose. According to records, Honsha was awarded the rank of 4th rank in the 16th year of the Jogan era. This effectively means that he was ranked higher than the fifth rank, which was appointed as {{ill|lt=Shimosa Province|Q1053695|WD=Q1053695|1=Shimōsa Province}}{{ill|lt=Kokushi|Q1351234|WD=Q1351234|1=Kokushi (official)}}, and shows that the head office was positioned as an important shrine at that time. However, there is no clear reason why he was given such a high rank. However, it is generally believed that they were trying to increase the influence of {{ill|lt=Yamato Dynasty|Q2658252|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Dynasty|1=Yamato Kingship}} by bestowing a high rank on the headquarters, which was highly worshiped by the residents of this region. }} {{Right|[[Image:tomeidaiⅱ.jpg|thumb|none|Lighthouse distant view]]}} === Precincts === === Setsusha === * '''Tokiwa Shrine'' (Setsusha) :{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}, and {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Hidetada|Q314464|WD=Q314464|lt=Tokugawa Hidetada|1=Tokugawa Hidetada}} are enshrined as deities. * '''{{ill|lt=Toyouke Daijingu|Q11633343|WD=Q11633343|lt=Geku|1=Toyōke Daijingū}}''' (Setsusha) :The enshrined deity is {{ill|lt=Toyoukebime|Q2983724|WD=Q2983724|lt=Toyoukehime Okami|1=Toyouke-hime}}. * '''{{ill|lt=Yakumo Shrine|Q11391847|WD=Q11391847|1=Yakumo shrine}}''' (Setsusha) :{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Susanoo no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} is the main deity, and {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Omi Takakami|1=Ōkuninushi}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kikiinada Hime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} are enshrined. * '''Ama no Onbashira Shrine'' (sub-sha) :Enshrines the {{ill|lt=Heroic Spirit|Q11617005|WD=Q11617005|1=eirei}} of the protector of the country. * '''Otori Shrine'' (Setsusha) :The enshrined deity is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru|1=UNKNOWN}}. * '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yatsurugi Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}・{{ill|lt=Yasaka Shrine|Q692714|WD=Q692714|1=Yasaka Shrine}}''' (Setsusha) :The enshrined deity is Susanoo no Mikoto and is enshrined in {{ill|lt=Mikoshi|Q979940|WD=Q979940|1=Mikoshi}}. * '''Funatama Shrine'' (sub-shrine) :{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amantorifune Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sankami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi Mikoto|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}} are the enshrined deities. It is said that it was originally dedicated to the {{ill|lt=ship spirit|Q11614362|WD=Q11614362|lt=ship spirit|1=ship spirit}}, and the shrine building is modeled after the shape of a ship. * '''{{ill|lt=Sengen Shrine|Q3471785|WD=Q3471785|1=Sengen shrine}}''' (sub-shrine):The enshrined deity is {{ill|lt=Konohana Sakuyabime|Q1781862|WD=Q1781862|lt=Konohana Sakuyabime no Mikoto|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}. It is enshrined on a hill in the northern part of the precincts. === Cultural assets === === Prefectural designated cultural property === * {{ill|lt=Funabashi Daijingu Lighthouse|Q11614129|WD=Q11614129|1=Funabashi Daijingū Tōmyōdai}} ({{ill|lt=List of Chiba Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties #Tangible Folk Cultural Properties|Q11406175|WD=Q11406175|lt=Chiba Prefecture Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties|1=Chiba Prefecture Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties}}) === City designated cultural property === * {{ill|lt=Kagura|Q1348260|WD=Q1348260|1=Kagura}} (City-designated intangible folk cultural property) === Event === === Dedicated Sumo at Funabashi Daijingu Shrine (October 20th) === The votive {{ill|lt=sumo|Q40561|WD=Q40561|1=Sumo}} held as an annual autumn festival has a long history, originating from {{ill|lt=Ieyasu Tokugawa|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}'s Kanran sumo held in {{ill|lt=1590|Q6764|WD=Q6764|1=1590}} ({{ill|lt=Tensho|Q1145058|WD=Q1145058|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)}}18). At that time, Ieyasu occasionally held falconry events in Shimousa, and had an annex set up as a lodging in {{ill|lt=Funabashi City|Q271417|WD=Q271417|lt=Funabashi|1=Funabashi}}. ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Funabashi Goten|1=UNKNOWN}} was located in what is now {{ill|lt=Funabashi City|Q271417|WD=Q271417|1=Funabashi}} Honmachi 4-chome, and was called "Gotenji." The former site is {{ill|lt=Funabashi Toshogu|Q11614238|WD=Q11614238|1=Funabashi-tōshōgū}}) One day, Ieyasu saw a child playing sumo. It is said that the origin of sumo is said to have been dedicated to Funabashi Daijingu Shrine, where people were deeply religious, and later on, {{ill|lt=Kanjin|Q6363447|WD=Q6363447|1=Kanjin}} himself became the origin of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=amateur sumo|1=UNKNOWN}}.Amateur sumo in Jingu is known for attracting strong wrestlers, and it still contributes to the training of {{ill|lt=sumo wrestlers|Q2727289|WD=Q2727289|1=Rikishi}} from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokatsu|1=UNKNOWN}}. Also, until recently, it was famous for the gathering of enthusiastic {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=spectators|1=UNKNOWN}}, including {{ill|lt=fishermen|Q331432|WD=Q331432|1=Fisherman}}, and spectators dissatisfied with the decisions would throw things and {{jal It was said that there was a scene where ink|Gyoji|Q907647}} was beaten up and he clashed with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=young people|1=UNKNOWN}} wearing {{ill|lt=Manju|Q11353895|WD=Q11353895|1=Manju}}, which caused a lot of excitement. === Photo === Image:oohijinjya5.jpg|Okumiya (currently Tokiwa Shrine) Image:oohijinjya7.jpg|War Cenotaph Image:oohijinjya1.jpg|Torii Image:oohijinja-dohyo.jpg|Dohyo ring File:Ojingu-shita intersection 20241014-P1058599.jpg|Ojingu-shita intersection === Transportation === nearest station * 5 minutes walk from {{ill|lt=Keisei Main Line|Q1063675|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Electric Railway Main Line|1=Keisei Main Line}}{{ill|lt=Ojingu-Shimo Station|Q5209145|WD=Q5209145|1=Daijingūshita Station}} * About 10 minutes walk from {{ill|lt=Sobu Main Line|Q1191364|WD=Q1191364|lt=JR Sobu Line|1=Sōbu Main Line}}{{ill|lt=Funabashi Station|Q800795|WD=Q800795|1=Funabashi Station}} === Related shrines === Efumi Shrine has the following branch shrines. '''Yonegasaki Town Etubi Shrine''' : 332 Yonegasakicho, Funabashi City, Chiba Prefecture : (Enshrined deity) Amaterasu Omikami : (Shrines within the precincts) Tenmangu Shrine, Inari Daimyojin, Dosojin, Kumano Daimyojin : Yonegasaki Castle was built during the Kamakura period. '''Higashimachi Ifuhi Shrine''' : 802 Higashimachi, Funabashi City, Chiba Prefecture : (Enshrined deity) Amaterasu Omikami : (Shrines within the precincts) Dewa Sanzan Daimyojin, Tenmangu, Dosojin === Its common name is ``Funabashi Daijingu'' (Funabashi Daijingu). In the Engishiki ceremony, it appears under the name ``Katsugo-gun Ifuhi Shrine.'' === Enshrined God === * '''{{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|1=Amaterasu}}''' ===Origin of company name=== There are various theories about the origin of the company's name, ``Ohhi, {{ill|lt=Historical kana usage|UNKNOWN|lt=Old kana usage}}: Ohohi. The main ones are shown below. * The theory that he is a food god, meaning a great fire or a great meal. * The theory is that it is a sunset because it is located on a hill that is directly facing the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sunset|1=UNKNOWN}} sun. * Theory that the {{ill|lt=guardian deity|Q767655|WD=Q767655|1=Ujigami}} of the {{ill|lt=Ta clan|Q11430816|WD=Q11430816|lt=Yitomi|1=Ō clan}}, an ancient and powerful ruling family. * This theory, which means Dainichi, is Otendo-sama (sun god), which {{ill|lt=farmers|Q838811|WD=Q838811|1=Peasant}} in this region had originally worshiped.{{efn|This theory was announced as a theory that added criticism and research to the previous theories, and attracted attention. As if to support this theory, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tendo Nenbutsu|1=UNKNOWN}} has been popular in the city since ancient times, and Daijingu Shrine also has a hanging Buddha statue representing the ``Dainichi Nyorai statue'' that was used before the {{ill|lt=Separation of Shinto and Buddhism|Shinto Buddhism Order|WD=Shinto Buddhism Order|ltq=Q1970535}} order was issued. }} === History === According to the shrine's legend, it began in the year 40 of {{ill|lt=Emperor Keiko|Q329723|WD=Q329723|1=Emperor Keikō}}, when {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru|1=UNKNOWN}} prayed for the pacification of the eastern region during his expedition to the east. At that time, the local residents were suffering from drought, and when Nihon Takeru prayed for rain at the same time, it was said that it started raining. Originally, the local sun god ``Itobijin (Dainichijin)'' was enshrined at the company, and it attracted the faith of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=fishermen|1=UNKNOWN}} in the surrounding area ({{ill|lt=Tokyo Bay|Q141017|WD=Q141017|1=Tokyo Bay}}). The first time I read {{ill|lt=Rokukokushi|Q1151168|WD=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi|1=Rikkokushi}} is in "{{ill|lt=Jihon Sandai Joroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}" (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōkan}}5 years ({{ill|lt=863 years|Q25052|WD=Q25052|1=863}}) In the article dated May 26, {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, it is listed as a small shrine.Later, this area was donated to {{ill|lt=Ise Jingu|Q687168|WD=Q687168|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} and {{ill|lt=Mikuriya|Q11488831|WD=Q11488831|1=mikuriya}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Natsumi Mikuriya|1=UNKNOWN}}), and Shinmeisha Shrine, which enshrines Amaterasu Omikami, the deity of Ise Grand Shrine, as its guardian, is now {{jalink|Hie Shrine} in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Natsumidai|1=UNKNOWN}}. (Natsumidai, Funabashi City) ||Hie Shrine}} However, with the decline of Mikuriya, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinmeisha|1=UNKNOWN}} also became obsolete and was enshrined at Ifuhi Shrine. After that, faith in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu no Omikami|1=UNKNOWN}} became stronger, and the name of Ifuhi Shrine was gradually forgotten, and it came to be called exclusively Funabashi Shinmei or Funabashi Daijingu. Until the Sengoku period, the powerful {{ill|lt=Chiba clan|Q2975237|WD=Q2975237|1=Chiba clan}} family {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tomi clan|1=UNKNOWN}}, who maintained power in this area, served as {{ill|lt=chief priest|Q11453500|WD=Q11453500|1=Gūji}}. Even now, he has changed his surname to Chiba, and members of the same family serve as {{ill|lt=chief priest|Q11453500|WD=Q11453500|1=Gūji}}. The shrine held many medieval documents, including the {{jalink|Ichikawa-Funabashi War|Q812} from the Boshin War that occurred during the {{ill|lt=Meiji Restoration|Q8707|WD=Q8707|1=Meiji Restoration}}. 56|Battle of Funabashi}} It was burnt down along with the shrine building, and only a few items remain today, including letters from Mitsutane Chiba and a document dating back many years called ``Funabashi Mikuriya Rokuga Goda Kazunoji.'' The main hall was rebuilt in 1896, and the worship hall was rebuilt in 1891. In 1872, it was elevated to the status of a prefectural shrine, and the name was restored to Ifuhi Shrine as recorded in the Engishiki Shinmyocho.It was revered by the imperial court and the shogunate, and members such as {{ill|lt=Taira no Masakado|Q1207652|WD=Q1207652|1=Taira no Masakado}}, {{ill|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|WD=Q242800|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, and {{ill|lt=Ieyasu Tokugawa|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}} donated shrine territories and built and renovated the shrine buildings. At Tokiwa Shrine in the grounds of the shrine, a wooden Ieyasu statue containing Ieyasu's tooth is enshrined. In modern times, successive emperors such as {{ill|lt=Emperor Meiji|Q174231|WD=Q174231|1=Emperor Meiji}}, {{ill|lt=Emperor Taisho|Q157052|WD=Q157052|1=Emperor Taishō}}, and {{ill|lt=Emperor Showa|Q34479|WD=Q34479|1=Hirohito}} have visited the shrine. === Rank salary === * {{ill|lt=863 years|Q25052|WD=Q25052|1=863}} (Jōkan 5th year) {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} confers {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Seigoi Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} * {{ill|lt=871|Q24754|WD=Q24754|1=871}} (13th year of Jogan) {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Senior Fifth Rank Upper|1=UNKNOWN}} awarded * {{ill|lt=874|Q23843|WD=Q23843|1=874}} (16th year of Jogan) Awarded {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank Lower|1=UNKNOWN}} {{efn|{{ill|lt=Nara period|Q189178|WD=Q189178|1=Nara period}}, systems regarding {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Jingi|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=rituals|1=UNKNOWN}} were put in place, and he began to receive generous protection from the Ritsuryo state. Also, from this time the custom (shakaku) of conferring official rank on gods (shrines) arose. According to records, Honsha was awarded the rank of 4th rank in the 16th year of the Jogan era. This effectively means that he was ranked higher than the fifth rank, which was appointed as {{ill|lt=Shimosa Province|Q1053695|WD=Q1053695|1=Shimōsa Province}}{{ill|lt=Kokushi|Q1351234|WD=Q1351234|1=Kokushi (official)}}, and shows that the head office was positioned as an important shrine at that time. However, there is no clear reason why he was given such a high rank. However, it is generally believed that they were trying to increase the influence of {{ill|lt=Yamato Dynasty|Q2658252|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Dynasty|1=Yamato Kingship}} by bestowing a high rank on the headquarters, which was highly worshiped by the residents of this region. }} {{Right|[[Image:tomeidaiⅱ.jpg|thumb|none|Lighthouse distant view]]}} === Precincts === === Setsusha === * '''Tokiwa Shrine'' (Setsusha) :{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|WD=Q171977|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}, and {{ill|lt=Tokugawa Hidetada|Q314464|WD=Q314464|lt=Tokugawa Hidetada|1=Tokugawa Hidetada}} are enshrined as deities. * '''{{ill|lt=Toyouke Daijingu|Q11633343|WD=Q11633343|lt=Geku|1=Toyōke Daijingū}}''' (Setsusha) :The enshrined deity is {{ill|lt=Toyoukebime|Q2983724|WD=Q2983724|lt=Toyoukehime Okami|1=Toyouke-hime}}. * '''{{ill|lt=Yakumo Shrine|Q11391847|WD=Q11391847|1=Yakumo shrine}}''' (Setsusha) :{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Susanoo no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} is the main deity, and {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Omi Takakami|1=Ōkuninushi}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kikiinada Hime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} are enshrined. * '''Ama no Onbashira Shrine'' (sub-sha) :Enshrines the {{ill|lt=Heroic Spirit|Q11617005|WD=Q11617005|1=eirei}} of the protector of the country. * '''Otori Shrine'' (Setsusha) :The enshrined deity is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru|1=UNKNOWN}}. * '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yatsurugi Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}・{{ill|lt=Yasaka Shrine|Q692714|WD=Q692714|1=Yasaka Shrine}}''' (Setsusha) :The enshrined deity is Susanoo no Mikoto and is enshrined in {{ill|lt=Mikoshi|Q979940|WD=Q979940|1=Mikoshi}}. * '''Funatama Shrine'' (sub-shrine) :{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amantorifune Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sankami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi Mikoto|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}} are the enshrined deities. It is said that it was originally dedicated to the {{ill|lt=ship spirit|Q11614362|WD=Q11614362|lt=ship spirit|1=ship spirit}}, and the shrine building is modeled after the shape of a ship. * '''{{ill|lt=Sengen Shrine|Q3471785|WD=Q3471785|1=Sengen shrine}}''' (sub-shrine):The enshrined deity is {{ill|lt=Konohana Sakuyabime|Q1781862|WD=Q1781862|lt=Konohana Sakuyabime no Mikoto|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}. It is enshrined on a hill in the northern part of the precincts. === Cultural assets === === Prefectural designated cultural property === * {{ill|lt=Funabashi Daijingu Lighthouse|Q11614129|WD=Q11614129|1=Funabashi Daijingū Tōmyōdai}} ({{ill|lt=List of Chiba Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties #Tangible Folk Cultural Properties|Q11406175|WD=Q11406175|lt=Chiba Prefecture Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties|1=Chiba Prefecture Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties}}) === City designated cultural property === * {{ill|lt=Kagura|Q1348260|WD=Q1348260|1=Kagura}} (City-designated intangible folk cultural property) === Event === === Dedicated Sumo at Funabashi Daijingu Shrine (October 20th) === The votive {{ill|lt=sumo|Q40561|WD=Q40561|1=Sumo}} held as an annual autumn festival has a long history, originating from {{ill|lt=Ieyasu Tokugawa|Q171977|WD=Q171977|1=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}'s Kanran sumo held in {{ill|lt=1590|Q6764|WD=Q6764|1=1590}} ({{ill|lt=Tensho|Q1145058|WD=Q1145058|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)}}18). At that time, Ieyasu occasionally held falconry events in Shimousa, and had an annex set up as a lodging in {{ill|lt=Funabashi City|Q271417|WD=Q271417|lt=Funabashi|1=Funabashi}}. ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Funabashi Goten|1=UNKNOWN}} was located in what is now {{ill|lt=Funabashi City|Q271417|WD=Q271417|1=Funabashi}} Honmachi 4-chome, and was called "Gotenji." The former site is {{ill|lt=Funabashi Toshogu|Q11614238|WD=Q11614238|1=Funabashi-tōshōgū}}) One day, Ieyasu saw a child playing sumo. It is said that the origin of sumo is said to have been dedicated to Funabashi Daijingu Shrine, where people were deeply religious, and later on, {{ill|lt=Kanjin|Q6363447|WD=Q6363447|1=Kanjin}} himself became the origin of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=amateur sumo|1=UNKNOWN}}.Amateur sumo in Jingu is known for attracting strong wrestlers, and it still contributes to the training of {{ill|lt=sumo wrestlers|Q2727289|WD=Q2727289|1=Rikishi}} from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokatsu|1=UNKNOWN}}. Also, until recently, it was famous for the gathering of enthusiastic {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=spectators|1=UNKNOWN}}, including {{ill|lt=fishermen|Q331432|WD=Q331432|1=Fisherman}}, and spectators dissatisfied with the decisions would throw things and {{jal It was said that there was a scene where ink|Gyoji|Q907647}} was beaten up and he clashed with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=young people|1=UNKNOWN}} wearing {{ill|lt=Manju|Q11353895|WD=Q11353895|1=Manju}}, which caused a lot of excitement. === Photo === Image:oohijinjya5.jpg|Okumiya (currently Tokiwa Shrine) Image:oohijinjya7.jpg|War Cenotaph Image:oohijinjya1.jpg|Torii Image:oohijinja-dohyo.jpg|Dohyo ring File:Ojingu-shita intersection 20241014-P1058599.jpg|Ojingu-shita intersection === Transportation === nearest station * 5 minutes walk from {{ill|lt=Keisei Main Line|Q1063675|WD=Q1063675|lt=Keisei Electric Railway Main Line|1=Keisei Main Line}}{{ill|lt=Ojingu-Shimo Station|Q5209145|WD=Q5209145|1=Daijingūshita Station}} * About 10 minutes walk from {{ill|lt=Sobu Main Line|Q1191364|WD=Q1191364|lt=JR Sobu Line|1=Sōbu Main Line}}{{ill|lt=Funabashi Station|Q800795|WD=Q800795|1=Funabashi Station}} === Related shrines === Efumi Shrine has the following branch shrines.
